title: Greetings and introductions
text: Lesson overview In this unit, you move from reading to communicating. You will learn the expressions Arabic speakers use to greet each other, introduce themselves and say goodbye in Modern Standard Arabic (MSA), as well as the difference between addressing a man and a woman, which you can hear in every question in Arabic. These are fixed expressions: learn them as complete chunks. You will explore the grammar behind them in later units. Item Details Code A1-01 Level A1 · Module A1.1 •Presentation of oneself • Prerequisites Level examination 0 exceeded Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 13 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-01), voice synthesis script, first session with the tutor (30 minutes) Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. healthy and respond to greetings at different times of the day, with the correct matched response; 2. to present yourself by name and ask the name of a man and a woman; 3. ask and tell how you are, choosing ⁧حَالُكَ⁩ or ⁧حَالُكِ⁩ according to who you are before; 4. thank you, apologize, dismiss you; 5. to recognize the formulas of daily use by God's name and to respond adequately; 6. read the transliteration of the volume, which follows the reading "in pause" Plan of the week. Day Activity 1 Section 0 · Dialogue 1 · lexicon (first half) 2 Sections 2–3: formulas and male/female · exercises 1–3 3 Dialogue 2 · section 4: pronunciation · exercises 4–5 4 Section 5: culture · examples in context · exercises 6–7 5 Reading and writing · exercises 8–9 6 Listening and oral production · session with the tutor 7 Unit verification · review Anki 0. How to read the Arabic of this volume From here on Arabic is printed in full vocalization , including the final vowels indicating the function of the word in the sentence (the case endings, which you will study in A1-19). Transliteration follows formal reading with a simple rule: • Inside the sentence everything is pronounced: ⁧كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟⁩ kayfa ḥāluka? ; • in pause, i.e. before a punctuation mark or at the end of the stroke, falls the last short vowel and the tanwīn - one/-in: ⁧بِخَيْرٍ⁩ read bi-ḫayr , ⁧السَّلَامُ⁩ read as-salām ; the ⁧ة⁩ read -a; • Suffix pronouns remain whole (-ka, -ki, -hu, -hā...), because they distinguish the meaning: ⁧حَالُكِ⁩ ḥāluki ; • tanwīn -an of formulas and adverbs remains -an also in pause: ⁧شُكْرًا⁩ šukran . In spontaneous speech, many Arabic speakers fail to hear the endings even within the sentence. In your oral productions of A1 It is not a mistake: it is important to speak the word well. 1. The formulas and their answers In Arabic many greetings have a fixed answer: the same formula is not repeated, it is answered with that paired. Learn them in pairs. The safest in the professional field ⁧صَبَاحُ الخَيْرِ⁩ ṣabāḥu l-ḫayr Morning of the good ⁧صَبَاحُ النُّورِ⁩ ṣabāḥu n-nūr Light morning Good morning, until about noon ⁧مَسَاءُ الخَيْرِ⁩ masāʾu l-ḫayr ⁧مَسَاءُ النُّورِ⁩ masāʾu n-nūr Good afternoon, good evening. ⁧مَرْحَبًا⁩ marḥaban ⁧مَرْحَبًا⁩ / ⁧أَهْلًا⁩ marḥaban / ahlan Hello, hello: neutral and informal ⁧أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا⁩ ahlan wa-sahlan ⁧أَهْلًا بِكَ⁩ / ⁧بِكِ⁩ ahlan bika / biki Welcome; It's telling who it comes to. ⁧كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟⁩ / ⁧كَيْفَ حَالُكِ؟⁩ kayfa ḥāluka / ḥāluki? ⁧بِخَيْرٍ، الحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ⁩ bi-ḫayr, al- ḥamdu li-llāh How are you? With salvation... ⁧تُصْبِحُ عَلَى خَيْرٍ⁩ / ⁧تُصْبِحِينَ⁩ ⁧وَأَنْتَ مِنْ أَهْلِهِ⁩ / ⁧وَأَنْتِ مِنْ⁩ Good night (to a man/a woman), before ⁧عَلَى خَيْرٍ⁩ tuṣbiḥu / tuṣbiḥīna ⁧أَهْلِهِ⁩ wa-anta / wa-anti min go to sleep ʿalā ḫayr ahlihi Because that's how it works. The paired formulas are a game of revival: to the "Peace" is answered with peace, to the "Bene" is answered with the "Luce" (light), which is something more. Responding with the right formula indicates that you know the rules of courtesy; repeating the same formula is understandable, but it sounds like a beginner. More words of courtesy. ⁧مِنْ فَضْلِكَ⁩ / ⁧مِنْ فَضْلِكِ⁩ min faḍlika / min faḍliki Please (to a man/woman) · ⁧آسِف⁩ / ⁧آسِفَة⁩ āsif / āsifa I'm sorry, I'm sorry (said by a man/woman), to whom you respond. ⁧لَا بَأْسَ⁩ lā baʾs It's okay. ⁧نَعَمْ⁩ naʿam "Yes" · ⁧لَا⁩ lā "No" is the name. Titles. ⁧أُسْتَاذ⁩ ustāḏ "Professor" is a teacher, but also a respectable one for an educated man; ⁧أُسْتَاذَة⁩ ustāḏa for a woman. ⁧سَيِّد⁩ Sayyid -- sir -- ⁧سَيِّدَة⁩ Sayyida ... ma'am... are used before the name: ⁧السَّيِّدُ كَرِيم⁩ as-sayyid Karīm . To call someone he puts on ⁧يَا⁩ yā in front of the name or title: ⁧يَا سَلْمَى⁩ yā Salmā , ⁧يَا أُسْتَاذُ⁩ yā ustāḏ . 3. Man or woman: your shape changes In Arabic, the "tu" has two forms: ⁧أَنْتَ⁩ door for a man and ⁧أَنْتِ⁩ anti for a woman. The same is true of the suffix "your": -ka for a man, -ki for a woman. Every formula addressed to a person therefore changes according to the listener. To a man To a woman Meaning ⁧كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟⁩ kayfa ḥāluka? ⁧كَيْفَ حَالُكِ؟⁩ kayfa ḥāluki? How are you? ⁧مَا اسْمُكَ؟⁩ mā Smuka? ⁧مَا اسْمُكِ؟⁩ mā Smuki? What's your name? (Lett. What about you? ⁧مِنْ فَضْلِكَ⁩ min faḍlika ⁧مِنْ فَضْلِكِ⁩ min faḍliki Please The formulas with -kum, how ⁧السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ⁩ • on you • they are plural but are also used with only one person : they are fixed. Instead, the shape changes according to who speaks in ⁧آسِف⁩ / : ⁧آسِفَة⁩ Luca says ⁧آسِف⁩ , Salmā says ⁧آسِفَة⁩ . Without verbs be. Pronunciation ⁧ع⁩ in formulas. ⁧عَلَيْكُمْ⁩ , ⁧عَفْوًا⁩ , ⁧مَعَ⁩ begin or contain ʿayn: it is a full consonant, with the compressed pharynx (L0-07). alaykum without ʿayn is the most recognizable mistake of an Italian. ⁧ح⁩ , ⁧خ⁩ and ⁧ه⁩ . ⁧حَال⁩ and ⁧الحَمْد⁩ have ḥāʾ, deaf African of the faringe, without scrape; ⁧خَيْر⁩ has ḫāʾ, with the scraper at the bottom of the mouth; ⁧أَهْلًا⁩ has hāʾ, a light aspiration. Three different sounds in three formulas you will use every day. Solar letters. ⁧السَّلَام⁩ as-salām and ⁧النُّور⁩ an-nūr assimilate the article; ⁧الخَيْر⁩ al-ḫayr and ⁧الحَمْد⁩ al-ḥamd no (L0-04). The support vowel. In ⁧وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ⁩ the word ⁧عَلَيْكُمْ⁩ ends without vowel and the next begins with an aliif waṣla: To tie them you add a vowel, here u: wa-ʿalaykumu s-salām . It's the same rule of ⁧عَنِ التَّحْقِيقِ⁩ in L0-09. . ⁧الله⁩ The double Allāh It is veiled, darkened [ɫɫ], after a and u: Allāh , šāʾa llāh . After the news is clear: li-llāh in ⁧الحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ⁩ . The tanwīn -an. In ⁧شُكْرًا⁩ , ⁧عَفْوًا⁩ , ⁧مَرْحَبًا⁩ the final alif is only the support of tanwīn: you read -an , not -ā Long. 6. Culture and register The safest greeting. ⁧السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ⁩ is understood and used throughout the Arab world, by Muslims and, in many areas, also by Christians. In a professional context with interlocutors you do not know is the safest choice; ⁧صَبَاحُ الخَيْرِ⁩ and ⁧مَسَاءُ الخَيْرِ⁩ They're neutral and they're good everywhere. ⁧مَرْحَبًا⁩ is friendly: use it with colleagues and peers. Formulas with the name of God. ⁧الحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ⁩ , ⁧إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ⁩ and ⁧مَا شَاءَ اللهُ⁩ mā šāʾa llāh The one that God wanted (admiration for something beautiful or successful) are part of the daily language of Arabic speakers of every religion and degree of religiosity. Using them is normal and appreciated; It's not rude. Recognizing them is indispensable: they recur in every conversation and in many texts. The handshake. Among men it is normal and often long. With a woman she lets her hand first: some people, out of religious conviction, do not shake hands with the opposite sex and greet by carrying their right hand to the chest. It is not an offense and should not be commented on. The dialects, just to recognize them. In the daily talk, how are you doing?It changes from country to country. Do not use these forms in exercises: they are used to avoid being distraught. Area How are you? Good. title: Single personal pronouns and nominal phrase
text: Lesson overview The Italian says "I'm a cop." Arabic says "Cops": . ⁧أَنَا شُرْطِيٌّ⁩ At present there is no verb "to be" and the phrase is based on two names placed next to each other. It is the nominal phrase, the most frequent structure of written Arabic. In this unity learn the singular pronouns and words to present yourself and others: who they are, what work they do, where they come from. Item Details Code A1-02 Level A1 · Module A1.1 •Presentation of oneself • Prerequisites A1-01 exceeded Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 14 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-02), script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. use the five singular pronouns ⁧أَنَا، أَنْتَ، أَنْتِ، هُوَ، هِيَ⁩ ; 2. build nominal sentences to the present without verb "to be" ; 3. tell your work and that of other people, male and female; 4. tell where you come from with ⁧مِنْ⁩ , even before the article ( ⁧مِنَ القَاهِرَةِ⁩ ); 5. understand short presentations read or heard and present three people. Plan of the week. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · section 2: the pronouns · vocabulary 2 Section 3: the nominal sentence · exercises 1–3 3 Sections 4–5: undetermined and determined, ⁧مِنْ⁩ · financial years 4–5 4 Dialogue 2 · pronunciation · examples in context · exercises 6–7 5 Reading · exercise 8 · writing 6 Listening · Oral production with tutor 7 Unit verification · review Anki 1. Dialogue 1 · The first day of the course Salmā Asks every student to show up. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧أَنَا سَلْمَى، وَأَنَا⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧وَأَنْتَ؟⁩ . ⁧مُدَرِّسَةٌ⁩ Salmā: anā Salmā, wa-anā mudarrisa. wa-anta? Salmā: I am Salmā And I'm a teacher. What about you? . ⁧أَنَا شُرْطِيٌّ⁩ . ⁧أَنَا لُوكَا⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: anā Lūkā. anā šurṭī. I'm Luca. I'm a cop. ⁧وَأَنْتِ؟⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: wa-anti? Salmā: What about you? Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧أَنَا مُهَنْدِسَةٌ⁩ . ⁧أَنَا مَارْيَا⁩ : ⁧مَارْيَا⁩ . ⁧مِنْ رُومَا⁩ Māryā: anā Māryā. anā muhandisatun min Rūmā. I'm Maria. I'm an engineer from Rome. ⁧وَأَنْتَ يَا أُسْتَاذُ؟⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: wa-anta yā ustāḏ? Salmā: And you, sir? ⁧أَنَا طَبِيبٌ⁩ . ⁧أَنَا أَحْمَد⁩ : ⁧أَحْمَد⁩ ⁧مِنْ سُورِيَا، وَأَنَا طَالِبٌ هُنَا⁩ . ⁧أَيْضًا⁩ Aḥmad: anā Aḥmad. anā ṭabībun min Sūriyā, wa-anā ṭālibun hunā ayḍan. Ahmad: I'm Ahmad. I am a Syrian doctor (Lett. from Syria) and here I am also student. What to notice. No bar contains ... are... ⁧أَنَا شُرْطِيٌّ⁩ It's a complete sentence. Ahmad was born in Syria but grew up in Italy: he speaks the family dialect and attends the course to learn Arabic standard, a frequent situation among Arabic speakers of the second generation. Salmā addresses him with ⁧أَنْتَ⁩ even if we would use the standard Arabic in English: it does not have a pronoun of courtesy; respect is expressed by the title ( ⁧يَا أُسْتَاذُ⁩ ) and with formulas. 2. The singular personal pronouns Proname Transliteration Meaning Note ⁧أَنَا⁩ anā me Man or woman. The final alif is written but in the speech the a is often short: [ʔana] ⁧أَنْتَ⁩ anta You (to a man) It's written as ⁧أَنْتِ⁩ : only the final vowel distinguishes them ⁧أَنْتِ⁩ anti You (to a woman) In texts without vowels decides the context ⁧هُوَ⁩ huwa him; it Even for masculine things ⁧هِيَ⁩ Hiya her; it also for things of female gender Because gender is important. In Arabic, every name is male or female, and the pronouns "he/she" also apply to things: ⁧الكِتَابُ؟ هُوَ هُنَا⁩ Is it the book? It is (Lett. It) here. You'll see better in A1-03. The final vowels of the pronouns never fall. The pause rule (A1-01Section 0) is about desinences, not pronouns: it always says door, anti, huwa, hiya, even at the end of sentence. In texts without vowels ⁧أنت⁩ it can be anta or anti: it is decided who is the person you are talking about. 3. The nominal sentence A nominal sentence has two parts: the subject (in Arabic ⁧مُبْتَدَأ⁩ mubtadaʾ , "what you begin with") and the predicate ( ⁧خَبَر⁩ ḫabar , • information •). At present there is no verb between the two parts. Subject Predicted Translation  ⁧طَالِبٌأَنَا⁩ I am a student  ⁧طَبِيبَةٌهِيَ⁩ You're a doctor.  ⁧طَبِيبٌأَحْمَد⁩ Ahmad is a doctor ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧هُنَا⁩ Salmā is here ⁧هُوَ⁩ ⁧مِنْ سُورِيَا⁩ He's from Syria How it works. Arabic considers the link between subject and predicate to the present evident, and does not express it. The verb "to be" appears only when it is necessary to indicate a different time (past, future: A2) or in particular constructions. For this reason, do not insert anything between the subject and the predicate: ⁧أَنَا هُوَ طَالِبٌ⁩ It's wrong. The deal. The predicate agrees in general with the subject: ⁧هُوَ طَالِبٌ⁩ , ⁧هِيَ طَالِبَةٌ⁩ . The feminine of almost all professional names is formed by ⁧ة⁩ . Use it in this unit; in A1-03 You'll see the rules and exceptions. The predicate does not have the article. In ⁧أَنَا طَالِبٌ⁩ "I'm a student" is the predicate indeterminate: ⁧الـ⁩ and with the tanwīn (-one), which corresponds to our . Arabic does not have a word for "un" . 4. Undetermined and determined Phrase Reading Meaning . ⁧أَنَا شُرْطِيٌّ⁩ anā šurṭī. I'm a cop (I say my job). . ⁧أَنَا الشُّرْطِيُّ⁩ anā š-šurṭī. I'm the cop (the one we talk about). . ⁧هِيَ مُدَرِّسَةٌ⁩ Hiya mudarrisa. You're a teacher. . ⁧هِيَ المُدَرِّسَةُ⁩ Hiya l-mudarrisa. You are the teacher (of the course). The article identifies a person already known (I am the one there); without article describes it . In modules and presentations, indeterminate predicate is almost always used. 5. Where you come from: ⁧مِنْ⁩ ⁧مِنْ⁩ min .'da, followed by the name of a country or city, indicates where: ⁧أَنَا مِنْ إِيطَالِيَا⁩ anā min Īṭāliyā I'm Italian, I'm from Italy. Before the Article ⁧مِنْ⁩ Take vowel to: ⁧مِنَ القَاهِرَةِ⁩ mina l-Qāhira From Cairo ⁧مِنَ المَغْرِبِ⁩ mina l-Maġrib From Morocco. It's the vowel of support you know from ⁧عَنِ التَّحْقِيقِ⁩ , but for ⁧مِنْ⁩ It's always in. Names of countries with the article. Some countries have the article in the name: ⁧القَاهِرَة⁩ (Cairo), ⁧المَغْرِب⁩ (Morocco), ⁧العِرَاق⁩ (Iraq), ⁧السُّودَان⁩ (Sudan). Other not: ⁧مِصْر⁩ (Egypt), ⁧سُورِيَا⁩ (Syria), ⁧لُبْنَان⁩ (Lebanon), ⁧تُونِس⁩ (Tunisia, Tunis), ⁧إِيطَالِيَا⁩ , ⁧رُومَا⁩ , ⁧مِيلَانُو⁩ . You learn them as whole words; in A1-07 You will pass from Egypt to Egyptian. The proper names are printed without the final vowel of the case ( ⁧يُوسُف⁩ , ⁧أَحْمَد⁩ , ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ), as they usually read; in the vocation with ⁧يَا⁩ take -u: . ⁧يَا كَرِيمُ⁩ 6. Dialogue 2 · A new colleague Karīm meets Hudā, cop just got to the office. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧أَنَا كَرِيم،⁩ . ⁧صَبَاحُ الخَيْرِ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ . ⁧وَأَنَا مُتَرْجِمٌ هُنَا⁩ Karīm: ṣabāḥu l-ḫayr. anā Karīm, wa-anā mutarǧimun hunā. KarīmMorning. I'm KarīmI'm an interpreter here. ⁧أَنَا⁩ . ⁧أَنَا هُدَى⁩ . ⁧صَبَاحُ النُّورِ⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ . ⁧شُرْطِيَّةٌ جَدِيدَةٌ⁩ Hudā: ṣabāḥu n-nūr. anā Hudā. anā šurṭiyyatun ǧadīda. HudāMorning. I'm Hudā. I'm a new cop. . ⁧أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا يَا هُدَى⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ Karīm: ahlan wa-sahlan yā Hudā. Karīm: Welcome, Hudā. ⁧وَهُوَ؟⁩ . ⁧أَهْلًا بِكَ⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ Hudā: ahlan bika. wa-huwa? Hudā: Thank you. What about him? . ⁧هُوَ لُوكَا، هُوَ شُرْطِيٌّ أَيْضًا⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ Karīm: huwa Lūkā, huwa šurṭiyyun ayḍan. Karīm: This is Luca, he's a cop too. . ⁧لُوكَا صَدِيقِي⁩ Lūkā ṣadīqī. Luca's my friend. What to notice. ⁧صَدِيقِي⁩ ṣadīqī My friend uses the suffix -ī of ⁧اِسْمِي⁩ . For a friend: ⁧صَدِيقَتِي⁩ ṣadīqatī , ⁧ة⁩ which becomes ⁧ت⁩ before the suffix (L0-10). In ⁧شُرْطِيَّةٌ جَدِيدَةٌ⁩ the adjective follows the name and takes the female: you will study it in A1-03. 7. Pronunciation The ⁧هُوَ⁩ and ⁧هِيَ⁩ . Italians tend not to pronounce it: uwa, iya. ⁧ه⁩ It is a consonant: a light but audible breath [h]. Do not confuse it with ⁧ح⁩ of ⁧حَال⁩ , more tense and without vibration. The šadda -iyy final. ⁧شُرْطِيٌّ⁩ , ⁧صَحَفِيٌّ⁩ , ⁧جُنْدِيٌّ⁩ end up in ⁧ـيّ⁩ with šadda. Inside the sentence you can hear the double: šurṭiyyun ; pause becomes a ī long: šurṭī . To the female, the double always remains: ⁧شُرْطِيَّة⁩ šurṭiyya . The emphasis in the professions. ⁧طَالِب⁩ and ⁧طَبِيب⁩ begin with ṭāʾ: the tongue leans behind the teeth, the back retreats towards the throat and the ā the following darkens [ɑː]. In ⁧مُوَظَّف⁩ c'è ẓāʾ double, emphatic and dental: muwaẓẓaf . ⁧مِنَ⁩ + Article. mina l-Qāhira It's just one rhythmic unit: don't stop after min. 8. Examples in context Example Transliteration Translation Note . ⁧أَنَا مُوَظَّفَةٌ فِي الوِزَارَةِ⁩ anā muwaẓẓafatun fī l-wizāra. I'm an employee in the ministry. He's a Lebanese journalist. Country name without item . ⁧أَنَا مِنَ المَغْرِبِ⁩ anā mina l-Maġrib. I'm Moroccan. ⁧مِنَ⁩ in front of the article . ⁧أَنْتِ زَمِيلَتِي⁩ anti zamīlatī. You're my partner. ⁧ة⁩ → ⁧ت⁩ before -ī . ⁧أَنَا الطَّبِيبُ⁩ anā ṭ-ṭabīb. I'm the doctor. Determined predicate: identify ⁧سَلْمَى هُنَا، وَأَحْمَد⁩ . ⁧هُنَاكَ⁩ Salmā hunā, wa-Aḥmad hunāk. Salmā It's here and Ahmad is there. Predicted adverb ⁧هُوَ جُنْدِيٌّ، وَهِيَ⁩ . ⁧مُمَرِّضَةٌ⁩ huwa ǧundiyyun, wa-hiya mumarriḍa. He's a soldier and she's a nurse.  11. Reading Luca presents the course group. ⁧يُوسُف طَالِبٌ، وَهُوَ⁩ . ⁧سَلْمَى مُدَرِّسَتِي، وَهِيَ مِنَ القَاهِرَةِ⁩ . ⁧أَنَا لُوكَا، وَأَنَا شُرْطِيٌّ فِي مِيلَانُو⁩ ⁧أَحْمَد⁩ . ⁧كَرِيم مُتَرْجِمٌ مِنَ المَغْرِبِ، وَهُوَ زَمِيلِي⁩ . ⁧مَارْيَا مُهَنْدِسَةٌ، وَهِيَ مِنْ رُومَا⁩ . ⁧مِنْ تُونِسَ⁩ . ⁧طَبِيبٌ مِنْ سُورِيَا، وَهُوَ صَدِيقِي أَيْضًا⁩ 13. Listening Script A · Dialog 1 ⁧وَأَنْتَ⁩ . ⁧أَنَا مُهَنْدِسَةٌ مِنْ رُومَا⁩ . ⁧وَأَنْتِ؟ أَنَا مَارْيَا⁩ . ⁧أَنَا شُرْطِيٌّ⁩ . ⁧وَأَنْتَ؟ أَنَا لُوكَا⁩ . ⁧أَنَا سَلْمَى، وَأَنَا مُدَرِّسَةٌ⁩ . ⁧أَنَا طَبِيبٌ مِنْ سُورِيَا، وَأَنَا طَالِبٌ هُنَا أَيْضًا⁩ . ⁧يَا أُسْتَاذُ؟ أَنَا أَحْمَد⁩ Script B · Four presentations . ⁧أَنَا صَحَفِيَّةٌ مِنْ بَيْرُوتَ⁩ . ⁧أَنَا نَادِيَة⁩ . ⁧مَسَاءُ الخَيْرِ⁩ . ⁧١⁩ . ⁧أَنَا مُمَرِّضٌ فِي المُسْتَشْفَى، وَأَنَا مِنَ القَاهِرَةِ⁩ . ⁧أَنَا عُمَر⁩ . ⁧٢⁩ . ⁧هُوَ زَمِيلِي، هُوَ مُهَنْدِسٌ⁩ . ⁧أَنَا سَارَة، وَأَنَا مُتَرْجِمَةٌ⁩ . ⁧السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ⁩ . ⁧٣⁩ . ⁧اِسْمِي سَمِير⁩ . ⁧أَنَا طَالِبٌ مِنَ المَغْرِبِ⁩ . ⁧٤⁩ 14. Oral production 1. Shadowing. Repeat the A script by overlapping the voice to the vocal synthesis; cure h of ⁧هُوَ⁩ and ⁧هِيَ⁩ . 2. Three people. Presents the three persons in the exercise without reading 9. Recorded: maximum 40 seconds. 3. With the tutor. The tutor shows you photos or names of characters invented with profession and city; you present them with ⁧هُوَ⁩ / . ⁧هِيَ⁩ Then reverse the roles: the tutor shows up and you summarize it ⁧هُوَ⁩ / ⁧هِيَ⁩ …». 15. Typical errors Error Correction ⁧أَنَا هُوَ طَالِبٌ⁩ (I'm in the middle of the picture) : ⁧أَنَا طَالِبٌ⁩ to the present there is no verb "to be" ⁧هِيَ طَالِبٌ⁩ : ⁧هِيَ طَالِبَةٌ⁩ the predicate agrees in genre ⁧مِنْ القَاهِرَةِ⁩ , min bed al-Qāhira ⁧مِنَ القَاهِرَةِ⁩ mina l-Qāhira uwa , iya huwa, hiya: the h is pronounced Error Correction ⁧أَنَا الطَّالِبُ⁩ to say your job : ⁧أَنَا طَالِبٌ⁩ The article changes the way I am the student Look for a pronoun of courtesy for you In MSA it is used ⁧أَنْتَ⁩ / ⁧أَنْتِ⁩ , with title and formulas Translate ⁧طَالِبٌ⁩ with the student tanwīn indicates the indeterminate: "one student" 16. Flashcard Deck A1, tag A1-02: 28 rumors. For the professions, the paper shows the male: before turning it say aloud also the female. 17. Unit verification Twenty points; Exceeding at least 16. You (man) are a Journalist. · 9. Hudā She's a cop. · 10. Karīm He's my partner. C · Determination (2 (paragraphs) 11. . ⁧أَنَا المُتَرْجِمُ⁩ · 12. . ⁧أَنَا مُتَرْجِمٌ⁩ D · Correction (4 (paragraphs) (i) correct: 13. . ⁧هِيَ مُهَنْدِسٌ⁩ · 14. . ⁧أَنَا هُوَ طَبِيبٌ⁩ · 15. ⁧مِنْ المَغْرِبِ⁩ · 16. title: Male and female, concordance of the adjective
text: Lesson overview Each Arabic name is masculine or feminine, and the adjective follows: ⁧مَدِينَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ⁩ A big city. ⁧بَيْتٌ كَبِيرٌ⁩ It's a big house. This unity teaches you to recognize gender, to form feminine and to describe people, places and objects. It lasts two weeks: the first for the rules, the second to enlarge the descriptive vocabulary and write the first descriptions. Item Details Code A1-03 Level A1 · Module A1.1 •Presentation of oneself • Prerequisites A1-02 exceeded Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 15–16 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-03), voice synthesis script, tutor session in the second week Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. recognize the kind of a name by form and know the female without ⁧ة⁩ more frequent; 2. to form the female adjectives and professional names; 3. put the adjective after the name and accord it in the genre, even with two adjectives; 4. Use the adjective as a predicate ( ⁧هِيَ طَوِيلَةٌ⁩ ) and strengthen it with ⁧جِدًّا⁩ ; 5. describe two people and one city in 40 words; 6. recognize when listening if you talk about a man or a woman. Two-week plan. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · section 2: the kind of names 2 Section 3: women without ⁧ة⁩ · financial years 1–2 3 Section 4: train female · exercise 3 4 Section 5: the agreement of the adjective · exercises 4–5 5 Pronunciation · lexicon (first half) · exercise 6 6 Listening: script A and B · exercise 10 7 Review Anki · rereading the dialogue 1 8 Dialogue 2 · section 6: more adjectives, ⁧جِدًّا⁩ , ⁧لٰكِنْ⁩ 9 Vocabulary (second half) · examples in context · exercises 6–7 10 Reading · exercise 8 11 Writing · Exercise 9 12 Session with the tutor: describe 13 Unit verification 14 Recovery of weaknesses · Anki 1. Dialogue 1 · A family photo After the lesson Salmā Show Luca a picture on the phone. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧مَنْ هِيَ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: man hiya? Who are you? ⁧هِيَ مُدَرِّسَةٌ⁩ . ⁧هِيَ أُمِّي⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ . ⁧أَيْضًا⁩ Salmā: hiya ummī. hiya mudarrisatun ayḍan. Salmā: She is my mother. She's a teacher, too. ⁧وَمَنْ هُوَ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-man huwa? Luca: And who is he? ⁧هُوَ صَغِيرٌ، وَهُوَ⁩ . ⁧هُوَ أَخِي⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ . ⁧طَالِبٌ فِي الجَامِعَةِ⁩ Salmā: huwa aḫī. huwa ṣaġīrun, wa- huwa ṭālibun fī l-ǧāmiʿa. Salmā: He is my brother. He is young and a student at the university. ⁧وَالبِنْتُ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-l-bint? What about the baby? ⁧هِيَ صَغِيرَةٌ⁩ . ⁧هِيَ بِنْتِي⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ . ⁧جِدًّا⁩ Salmā: hiya bintī. hiya ṣaġīratun ǧiddan. Salmā: She is my daughter. It's very small. . ⁧هِيَ جَمِيلَةٌ⁩ ! ⁧مَا شَاءَ اللهُ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: mā šāʾa llāh! hiya ǧamīla. Luke: How beautiful, God bless you! It's beautiful. What to notice. ⁧مَنْ⁩ You'll study it in A1-06: here is a fixed block. ⁧صَغِيرٌ⁩ the name of the brother means "young" or "little girl." ⁧أُمِّي⁩ , ⁧أَخِي⁩ , ⁧بِنْتِي⁩ have the suffix -ī Mine/my. Luca uses ⁧مَا شَاءَ اللهُ⁩ ( A1-01) to compliment the child: it is the usual way of praising a child without attracting the evil eye, an attention widespread in many Arab families. 2. The kind of names In Arabic there is no neutral: every name is male ( ⁧مُذَكَّر⁩ muḏakkar ) or female ( ⁧مُؤَنَّث⁩ muʾannaṯ ). Male does not have a particular sign; women, in the vast majority of cases, end up ⁧ة⁩ . Masculine Feminine Meaning  ⁧طَالِبَةطَالِب⁩ student · student  ⁧مُدَرِّسَةمُدَرِّس⁩ teacher (man · woman)  ⁧مَدِينَةبَيْت⁩ home · city  ⁧جَامِعَةكِتَاب⁩ book · university ⁧سَيَّارَةمَكْتَب⁩ office · automobile The rule of thumb. A word that ends in ⁧ة⁩ is female; a word without ⁧ة⁩ is male, except for the exceptions of the section 3. The kind of things doesn't coincide with Italian: ⁧كِتَاب⁩ Book is male as in English, but ⁧شَمْس⁩ is female; and ⁧حَرْب⁩ It's also war. 3. Female without ⁧ة⁩ and male with ⁧ة⁩ They are a few words, but very frequent. Learn them by their kind. Group Examples Why Women for ⁧أُمّ⁩ ummm madre · ⁧بِنْت⁩ bint girl, daughter · ⁧أُخْت⁩ The meaning is feminine: ⁧ة⁩ no nature is needed uḫt sister Group Examples Why Females by tradition ⁧شَمْس⁩ šams sun · ⁧أَرْض⁩ arḍ soil · ⁧حَرْب⁩ ḥarb war · ⁧دَار⁩ dār home, seat · ⁧نَار⁩ nār fire They should be stored (in Anki they are marked "f." Double body parts ⁧يَد⁩ yad hand · ⁧عَيْن⁩ ʿayn eye Almost all parts of the body that are in pairs are female Cities and almost all countries ⁧القَاهِرَة⁩ · ⁧مِيلَانُو⁩ · ⁧سُورِيَا⁩ · ⁧مِصْر⁩ Place names are usually female; exceptions: ⁧المَغْرِب⁩ , ⁧العِرَاق⁩ , ⁧لُبْنَان⁩ , ⁧السُّودَان⁩ , ⁧الأُرْدُنّ⁩ Men with ⁧حَمْزَةة⁩ Ḥamza · ⁧أُسَامَة⁩ Usāma · ⁧خَلِيفَة⁩ ḫalīfa The meaning is masculine: the agreement is masculine caliph ( ⁧حَمْزَة طَالِبٌ⁩ ) Because you need it. In reading their own names, in A2, you'll see ⁧حَمْزَة⁩ and ⁧أُسَامَة⁩ are common male names: do not attribute them to a woman for ⁧ة⁩ Final. 4. Forming the Female For adjectives and person names you add ⁧ة⁩ to the male. In front of the ⁧ة⁩ the last consonant takes the fatḥa. Masculine Feminine Transliteration  ⁧كَبِيرَةكَبِير⁩ kabīr · kabīra  ⁧جَدِيدَةجَدِيد⁩ ǧadīd · ǧadīda  ⁧مُهِمَّةمُهِمّ⁩ muhimm · muhimma  ⁧شُرْطِيَّةشُرْطِيّ⁩ šurṭī · šurṭiyya  ⁧جَيِّدَةجَيِّد⁩ ǧayyid · ǧayyida  ⁧مَشْغُولَةمَشْغُول⁩ mašġūl · mašġūla Attention to the words in -iyy and the šadda. In ⁧مُهِمّ⁩ and ⁧شُرْطِيّ⁩ the šadda remains and the fatḥa go over the double letter: ⁧مُهِمَّة⁩ , ⁧شُرْطِيَّة⁩ . Exception to recognize. The adjectives of color and physical defect have a different feminine: ⁧أَحْمَر⁩ aḥmar Red-red → ⁧حَمْرَاء⁩ ḥamrāʾ . You will study them in A2; For now know that they exist. The ⁧ة⁩ paused and connected. In pause we read -a ( ⁧كَبِيرَة⁩ kabīra ); Inside the sentence one reads -at more desinence ( ⁧كَبِيرَةٌ جِدًّا⁩ kabīratun ǧiddan ). 5. The Adjective's Agreement Attributional adjective. It follows the name, always, and takes its kind (and desinence, which here is -a): Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧بَيْتٌ كَبِيرٌ⁩ baytun kabīr a big house ⁧مَدِينَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ⁩ madīnatun kabīra a big city ⁧طَالِبٌ جَدِيدٌ⁩ ṭālibun ǧadīd a new student ⁧طَالِبَةٌ جَدِيدَةٌ⁩ ṭālibatun ǧadīda a new student ⁧حَرْبٌ طَوِيلَةٌ⁩ ḥarbun ṭawīla a long war ( ⁧حَرْب⁩ is female) Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧أُمٌّ سَعِيدَةٌ⁩ ummun saʿīda a happy mother Predicted adjective. After a pronoun or proper name, the adjective itself forms the nominal phrase (A1-02): Arabic Transliteration Translation . ⁧هُوَ طَوِيلٌ⁩ huwa ṭawīl. He's tall. . ⁧هِيَ طَوِيلَةٌ⁩ hiya ṭawīla. She's tall. . ⁧أَنَا مَشْغُولَةٌ⁩ anā mašġūla. I'm busy (a woman speaks). . ⁧مِيلَانُو مَدِينَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ⁩ Mīlānū madīnatun ǧamīla. Milan is a beautiful city. Because the adjective goes later. In Arabic the name comes first and what qualifies it follows: it is a fixed order, not stylistic. Beautiful city with the adjective in front ( ⁧جَمِيلَةٌ مَدِينَةٌ⁩ ) is not an Arabic phrase. 6. Two adjectives, ⁧جِدًّا⁩ and ⁧لٰكِنْ⁩ More adjectives are put one after the other, all agreed: ⁧مَدِينَةٌ قَدِيمَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ⁩ It is an ancient and beautiful city. As preached they bind with ⁧وَ⁩ : ⁧القَاهِرَةُ كَبِيرَةٌ وَقَدِيمَةٌ⁩ . ⁧جِدًّا⁩ ǧiddan "Much" goes after the adjective: ⁧كَبِيرٌ جِدًّا⁩ Very big. It doesn't change for the genre. ⁧لٰكِنْ⁩ lākin "but" combines two sentences: . ⁧البَيْتُ صَغِيرٌ، لٰكِنْ هُوَ جَمِيلٌ⁩ In front of the article he took the support: ⁧لٰكِنِ الجَوُّ بَارِدٌ⁩ lākini l-ǧawwu bārid It's cold, though. The ā of ⁧لٰكِنْ⁩ is written with the short alif (L0-09). ⁧أَوْ⁩ aw .o., or ⁧طَوِيلٌ أَوْ قَصِيرٌ؟⁩ High or low? 7. Dialogue 2 · Milan and Cairo Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧القَاهِرَةُ كَبِيرَةٌ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: al-Qāhiratu kabīra? Is Cairo great? ⁧نَعَمْ، القَاهِرَةُ كَبِيرَةٌ جِدًّا،⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ . ⁧وَهِيَ قَدِيمَةٌ وَجَمِيلَةٌ⁩ Salmā: naʿam, al-Qāhiratu kabīratun ǧiddan, wa- hiya qadīmatun wa-ǧamīla. Salmā: Yes, Cairo is very large, and it is ancient and beautiful. ⁧مِيلَانُو جَمِيلَةٌ أَيْضًا، لٰكِنْ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ . ⁧هِيَ صَغِيرَةٌ⁩ Lūkā: Mīlānū ǧamīlatun ayḍan, lākin hiya ṣaġīra. Luca: Milan is beautiful too, but it's small. ⁧لَا، مِيلَانُو مَدِينَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ! ⁧أَيْضًا⁩ Salmā: lā, Mīlānū madīnatun kabīratun ayḍan! Salmā: No, Milan is also a great city! ⁧وَالجَوُّ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-l-ǧaww? What about the weather? ⁧الجَوُّ فِي القَاهِرَةِ حَارٌّ،⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ . ⁧وَفِي مِيلَانُو بَارِدٌ⁩ Salmā: al-ǧawwu fī l-Qāhirati ḥārrun, wa-fī Mīlānū bārid. Salmā: Cairo is hot, in Milan it's cold. ⁧وَالنِّيلُ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-n-nīl? What about the Nile? ⁧النِّيلُ طَوِيلٌ جِدًّا، وَهُوَ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ . ⁧جَمِيلٌ جِدًّا⁩ Salmā: an-nīlu ṭawīlun ǧiddan, wa-huwa ǧamīlun ǧiddan. Salmā: The Nile is very long and beautiful. What to notice. The cities are feminine: ⁧القَاهِرَةُ كَبِيرَةٌ⁩ , ⁧مِيلَانُو صَغِيرَةٌ⁩ . ⁧النِّيل⁩ is male: . ⁧طَوِيلٌ⁩ In ⁧النِّيلُ⁩ and ⁧الجَوُّ⁩ the article gives a name determined as subject: it is the structure of A1-04. 8. Pronunciation ⁧ة⁩ Inside the sentence. madīnatun kabīra : ⁧ة⁩ It is pronounced t when it follows desinence. Read madīna kabīra Inside a formal sentence is a reading error (acceptable only in the quick talk). Doubles. ⁧جِدًّا⁩ , ⁧حَارٌّ⁩ , ⁧مُهِمٌّ⁩ , ⁧جَيِّدٌ⁩ have the šadda: Keep the consonant twice as much as in English. ǧidan instead of ǧiddan It's a frequent mistake. ⁧ص⁩ and ⁧س⁩ . ⁧صَغِير⁩ ṣaġīr starts with ṣād emphasis: the following is dark, almost [ɑ]. ⁧سَعِيد⁩ saʿīd starts with sīn simple and has a ʿayn In the middle. ⁧غ⁩ in ⁧صَغِير⁩ . It is the airy/uvular sound fricativa of L0-07, not a g and not an Italian r. 9. title: Determination: Attributional and Predicative Adjective
text: Lesson overview ⁧البَيْتُ الكَبِيرُ⁩ means "the big house"; ⁧البَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ⁩ means "the house" is large. The difference lies in an article. In this unit you learn to distinguish the syntagma (name + adjective, a piece of phrase) from the nominal sentence (subject + predicate), to say It is the distinction that will allow you to read any newspaper title correctly. Two weeks. Item Details Code A1-04 Level A1 · Module A1.1 •Presentation of oneself • Prerequisites A1-03 exceeded Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 17–18 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-04), voice synthesis script, tutor session in the second week Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. distinguish definite and indefinite names (article, proper name, suffix); 2. grant the adjective also in determining: ⁧بَيْتٌ كَبِيرٌ⁩ / ⁧البَيْتُ الكَبِيرُ⁩ ; 3. build the nominal sentence with determined subject and predicate indefinitely: ⁧البَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ⁩ ; 4. say "c'è" with ⁧فِي⁩ ... and with ⁧هُنَاكَ⁩ where the entity is indeterminate; 5. recognize when listening if you hear a sentence or syntagma; 6. describe your neighbourhood in 50 words. Two-week plan. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · section 1: determined and indefinite 2 Section 2: the determined syntagma · exercises 1–2 3 Section 3: syntagma or phrase · exercise 3 4 Section 4: table of the four combinations · exercise 4 5 Pronunciation · lexicon (first half) · exercise 5 6 Listening: script B · exercise 10 7 Review Anki · reading aloud with intonation 8 Dialogue 2 · section 5: «c'è» 9 Section 6: suffix + adjective; prior toiḍāfa · financial years 6–7 10 Vocabulary (second half): the city · examples in context 11 Reading · exercise 8 12 Writing · session with tutor: in the city 13 Unit verification 14 Recovery of weaknesses · Anki 1. Dialogue 1 · The new office Karīm show to Hudā The offices of the department. Arabic Transliteration Translation . ⁧هُنَا المَكْتَبُ الجَدِيدُ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ Karīm: hunā l-maktabu l-ǧadīd. Karīm: Here (Lett. Here) the new office. ! ⁧المَكْتَبُ كَبِيرٌ وَجَمِيلٌ⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ Hudā: al-maktabu kabīrun wa-ǧamīl! Hudā: The office is great and beautiful! ⁧وَهُنَاكَ غُرْفَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ⁩ . ⁧نَعَمْ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ . ⁧وَغُرْفَةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ⁩ Karīm: naʿam. wa-hunāka ġurfatun kabīratun wa-ġurfatun ṣaġīra. Karīm: Yes. And there's a big room and a small room. ⁧وَالغُرْفَةُ الصَّغِيرَةُ؟⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ Hudā: wa-l-ġurfatu ṣ-ṣaġīra? Hudā: What about the small room? . ⁧الغُرْفَةُ الصَّغِيرَةُ مَكْتَبِي⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ . ⁧هِيَ هَادِئَةٌ جِدًّا⁩ Karīm: al-ġurfatu ṣ-ṣaġīratu maktabī. hiya hādiʾatun ǧiddan. KarīmThe small room is my office. It's very quiet. ⁧وَالسَّيَّارَةُ الجَدِيدَةُ؟⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ Hudā: wa-s-sayyāratu l-ǧadīda? Hudā: What about the new car? ⁧السَّيَّارَةُ فِي الشَّارِعِ،⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ Karīm: as-sayyāratu fī š-šāriʿ, wa-š-šāriʿu Karīm: The car is in the street, and the road is. ⁧وَالشَّارِعُ قَرِيبٌ⁩ qarīb. Neighbor. What to notice. ⁧المَكْتَبُ الجَدِيدُ⁩ The new office has the article on both words: it is a syntagma. ⁧المَكْتَبُ كَبِيرٌ⁩ The office is large , has the article only on the first: it is a sentence. In ⁧غُرْفَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ⁩ neither of them has the article: "A large room" 2. Determined and indefinite An Arabic name is indefinite ( ⁧نَكِرَة⁩ nakira) or determined ( ⁧مَعْرِفَة⁩ maʿrifa ). Type Sign Example Translation Indeterminate tanwīn (-un, -an, -in) ⁧بَيْتٌ⁩ baytun a house Determined by Article ⁧الـ⁩ , without tanwīn ⁧البَيْتُ⁩ al-baytu the house Own Name is determined by itself ⁧مِصْرُ⁩ , ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ , ⁧مِيلَانُو⁩ Milan, SalmāEgypt With possessive suffix the suffix determines ⁧بَيْتِي⁩ baytī my home A name cannot have article together and tanwīn : Either one or the other. In front of the suffix you do not put the article: "My house" is ⁧بَيْتِي⁩ , never ⁧البيتي⁩ ». 3. The syntagma: the adjective also copies the determination The attribute adjective agrees with the name in general (A1-03) and in determination: if the name has the article, the adjective also takes it. Indeterminate Determined Translation ⁧بَيْتٌ كَبِيرٌ⁩ baytun kabīr ⁧البَيْتُ الكَبِيرُ⁩ al-baytu l-kabīr a big house · the big house ⁧سَيَّارَةٌ جَدِيدَةٌ⁩ sayyāratun ǧadīda ⁧السَّيَّارَةُ الجَدِيدَةُ⁩ as-sayyāratu l-ǧadīda a new car · the new car ⁧شَارِعٌ ضَيِّقٌ⁩ šāriʿun ḍayyiq ⁧الشَّارِعُ الضَّيِّقُ⁩ aš-šāriʿu ḍ-ḍayyiq a narrow road · the narrow road ⁧مَدْرَسَةٌ قَدِيمَةٌ⁩ madrasatun qadīma ⁧المَدْرَسَةُ القَدِيمَةُ⁩ al-madrasatu l-qadīma an old school · the old school Because that's how it works. For Arabic the adjective is a name that repeats what precedes it: it follows it as an echo, with the same genre, the same determination and the same case. If the echo doesn't have the article while the name does, the link breaks and becomes another structure: the phrase. 4. Syntagma or phrase: the four combinations Arabic What is it? Translation ⁧بَيْتٌ كَبِيرٌ⁩ indeterminate syntagma a big house ⁧البَيْتُ الكَبِيرُ⁩ determined syntagma the big house ⁧البَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ⁩ sentence: determined subject + undetermined predicate the house is big ⁧البَيْتُ الكَبِيرُ جَمِيلٌ⁩ sentence: subject (determined syntagma) + predicate the big house is beautiful The golden rule of the nominal phrase. The subject is usually determined and the predicate undetermined. The point at which the determination is interrupted is the boundary between subject and predicate: in ⁧البَيْتُ الكَبِيرُ جَمِيلٌ⁩ the article reaches up to ⁧الكَبِيرُ⁩ , so the predicate is ⁧جَمِيلٌ⁩ . How to read it in a text without vowels. ⁧البيت الكبير⁩ = syntagma; ⁧البيت كبير⁩ = sentence. The article is also seen without vowels: it's your first analysis tool. To be recognized. When even the predicate is determined, a pronoun often fits between the two parts to mark the border: ⁧البَيْتُ هُوَ الكَبِيرُ⁩ The house is the big one. You'll meet him in the press. 5. There is, there are. An indefinite name does not normally open a nominal phrase. To say "there is a car in the street" it first puts the place: Arabic Transliteration Translation . ⁧فِي الشَّارِعِ سَيَّارَةٌ⁩ fī š-šāriʿi sayyāra. There's a car in the street. . ⁧فِي المَدِينَةِ جَامِعَةٌ قَدِيمَةٌ⁩ fī l-madīnati ǧāmiʿatun qadīma. There is an ancient university in the city. . ⁧هُنَاكَ مَسْجِدٌ فِي الشَّارِعِ⁩ hunāka masǧidun fī š-šāriʿ. There's a mosque in the street. ⁧هُنَاكَ صَيْدَلِيَّةٌ قَرِيبَةٌ؟⁩ hunāka ṣaydaliyyatun qarība? Is there a pharmacy nearby? Two streets. ⁧فِي⁩ + place + indeterminate name is the basic construction. ⁧هُنَاكَ⁩ , that in A1-02 It means "there" here it works as "there": it is very used in the media language. With a determined subject you return to the normal order: ⁧السَّيَّارَةُ فِي الشَّارِعِ⁩ The car is on the road. 6. Suffix + adjective; first look at theiḍāfa The name with suffix is determined , so the adjective takes the article: ⁧بَيْتِي الجَدِيدُ⁩ baytī l-ǧadīd My new home is in the middle of it. ⁧سَيَّارَتِي الصَّغِيرَةُ⁩ sayyāratī ṣ-ṣaġīra My little car is as preached, without article: ⁧بَيْتِي جَدِيدٌ⁩ My house is new. Name + name determined: liḍāfa. Two names next to each other, the first without article and the second determined, mean the first of the second: ⁧مَرْكَزُ الشُّرْطَةِ⁩ markazu š-šurṭa The police station is located in the centre of the city. The Centre of Police (CPD) ⁧وَسَطُ المَدِينَةِ⁩ wasaṭu l-madīna The city center is located in the city centre, ⁧بَابُ البَيْتِ⁩ bābu The door of the house is l-bayt. The first name is also determined without article. Recognize it for now: you will study it in A1-10. 7. Dialogue 2 · In the city Maria asks for information from a passerby. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧عَفْوًا، المَتْحَفُ قَرِيبٌ؟⁩ : ⁧مَارْيَا⁩ Māryā: ʿafwan, al-matḥafu qarīb? title: Demonstrationهٰذَا، هٰذِهِ، ذٰلِكَ، تِلْكَ‎
text: Lesson overview "What is this?" "This is my passport" "My passport," "That window" is big ": with the demos indicate objects and people." These are four very short words, but they change structure depending on whether you say "this" is a book "or this book": the same distinction between phrase and syntagma of A1-04. It's the last unit on the module. A1.1; The next week, we have the module test. Item Details Code A1-05 Level A1 · Module A1.1 •Presentation of oneself • Prerequisites A1-04 exceeded Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 19 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-05), voice synthesis scripts, real objects on the desk Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. use ⁧هٰذَا، هٰذِهِ، ذٰلِكَ، تِلْكَ⁩ second gender and distance; 2. distinguish ⁧هٰذَا كِتَابٌ⁩ This is a book from ⁧هٰذَا الكِتَابُ⁩ This book is the first book in the history of the world. 3. ask and answer  ? what is it? • who is it? ( ⁧مَا هٰذَا؟، مَنْ هٰذِهِ؟⁩ ); 4. appoint and describe the objects of an office and a bag; 5. understand indications about objects in a slow dialogue. Plan of the week. Salmā: And what is this? . ⁧هٰذِهِ وَرَقَةٌ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: hāḏihi waraqa. Luca: This is a sheet. ⁧وَذٰلِكَ؟⁩ ! ⁧أَحْسَنْتَ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: aḥsanta! wa-ḏālika? SalmāBravo! What about that? Salmā: What about that? . ⁧تِلْكَ نَافِذَةٌ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: tilka nāfiḏa. That's a window. ⁧هٰذَا الحَاسُوبُ⁩ . ⁧صَحِيحٌ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: ṣaḥīḥ. hāḏā l-ḥāsūbu ǧadīdun, Salmā: Right. This computer is ⁧جَدِيدٌ، لٰكِنْ تِلْكَ النَّافِذَةُ قَدِيمَةٌ⁩ lākin tilka n-nāfiḏatu qadīmatun ǧiddan! New, but that window is so old! ! ⁧جِدًّا⁩ What to notice. The demonstration follows the kind of Arabic, not Italian: ⁧وَرَقَة⁩ is female, so ⁧هٰذِهِ⁩ , even if in English we say "this sheet" is. Last line ⁧هٰذَا الحَاسُوبُ⁩ This computer is a syntagma, and ⁧جَدِيدٌ⁩ It's the predicate. 2. The four forms  Nearby (?) Away from the point of view of the area Masculine ⁧هٰذَا⁩ hāḏā ⁧ذٰلِكَ⁩ ḏālika Feminine ⁧هٰذِهِ⁩ hāḏihi ⁧تِلْكَ⁩ tilka Graffia. In ⁧هٰذَا⁩ , ⁧هٰذِهِ⁩ and ⁧ذٰلِكَ⁩ the ā long is written with the short aliph above the consonant (L0-09); in texts without vowels it disappears: . ⁧هذا، هذه، ذلك⁩ Writing ⁧هاذا⁩ It is an error of spelling, even if it is pronounced like this. For people and things. ⁧هٰذَا⁩ and ⁧هٰذِهِ⁩ apply to objects and persons: ⁧هٰذَا لُوكَا⁩ This is Luke. ⁧هٰذِهِ سَلْمَى⁩ This is Salmā». To be recognized. For more people you use ⁧هٰؤُلَاءِ⁩ hāʾulāʾi These, these, and ⁧أُولٰئِكَ⁩ ulāʾika "Those" are the following: you will study them with the plural in A1-12. For things in the plural, in Arabic, we use the singular female ⁧هٰذِهِ⁩ ( A1-15). 3. Phrase or syntagma: where the article stands Arabic Structure Translation . ⁧هٰذَا كِتَابٌ⁩ demo + indeterminate name = sentence This is a book. ⁧هٰذَا الكِتَابُ⁩ demo + name with article = syntagma this book . ⁧هٰذَا الكِتَابُ جَدِيدٌ⁩ syntagma + predicate = sentence This book is new. . ⁧هٰذَا هُوَ الكِتَابُ⁩ demo + pronoun + name determined = sentence This is the book (what you were looking for). . ⁧هٰذَا كِتَابِي⁩ demo + name with suffix = phrase This is my book. Because that's how it works. The demonstration is already determined. If the following name is indeterminate, there is a jump of determination and then a sentence boundary (as in ⁧البَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ⁩ , A1-04). If the name has the article, demonstrative and name form a single block: this book is ". To say "this" is the book "with a determined predicate," it inserts ⁧هُوَ⁩ / ⁧هِيَ⁩ to mark the border. With the suffix, the demo goes later. This my book is said to be ⁧كِتَابِي هٰذَا⁩ , and this city of Milan ⁧مَدِينَةُ مِيلَانُو هٰذِهِ⁩ : when the name is determined by a suffix or by aiḍāfaThe demo follows him. Recognize him; you will actively use it in A2. With an adjective. ⁧هٰذِهِ السَّيَّارَةُ الجَدِيدَةُ⁩ This new car is not covered by this Regulation. ⁧هٰذِهِ السَّيَّارَةُ جَدِيدَةٌ⁩ This car is new. title: Questions
text: Lesson overview Who? What? Where? When? How many? With this unit learn to ask questions and answer, and read and fill out a form with personal data. Arab questions have a rule that simplifies everything: they are always at the beginning of the sentence, and the rest does not change. For questions yes/no just put ⁧هَلْ⁩ in the face of a statement. Item Details Code A1-06 Level A1 · Module A1.2 "Ask and place" Prerequisites Module test A1.1 exceeded Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 21 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-06), script for speech synthesis, session with tutor Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. ask questions yes/no with ⁧هَلْ⁩ and answer with ⁧نَعَمْ⁩ / ⁧لَا⁩ ; 2. use ⁧مَا، مَاذَا، مَنْ، أَيْنَ، كَيْفَ، مَتَى، كَمْ، لِمَاذَا⁩ ; 3. ask and give personal data: first name, surname, age, address, work, telephone; 4. use ⁧كَمْ⁩ by the name to the singular: ⁧كَمْ طَالِبًا؟⁩ ; 5. read and fill out a simple form; 6. understand a slow interview and ask eight questions to the tutor. Plan of the week. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · sections 1–2: ⁧هَلْ⁩ and questions · lexicon (first half) 2 Section 3: ⁧مَا⁩ and ⁧مَاذَا⁩ · section 4: ⁧كَمْ⁩ · financial years 1–3 3 Section 5: personal data · reading the form · exercises 4–5 4 Dialogue 2 · pronunciation · lexicon (second half) · exercises 6–7 5 Writing: module and eight questions 6 Listening · session with the tutor: ask questions 7 Unit verification · review Anki 1. Are you an interpreter? ⁧نَعَمْ، أَنَا مُتَرْجِمٌ فِي مَرْكَزِ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ . ⁧الشُّرْطَةِ⁩ Karīm: naʿam, anā mutarǧimun fī markazi š-šurṭa. Karīm: Yes, I'm an interpreter at the police station. ⁧كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟⁩ : ⁧مَارْيَا⁩ Māryā: kam ʿumruka? How old are you? . ⁧عُمْرِي ثَلَاثُونَ سَنَةً⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ Karīm: ʿumrī ṯalāṯūna sana. Karīm: I am thirty years old. ⁧مَتَى الدَّرْسُ⁩ : ⁧سُؤَالٌ أَخِيرٌ⁩ : ⁧مَارْيَا⁩ ⁧القَادِمُ؟⁩ Māryā: suʾālun aḫīr: matā d-darsu l- qādim? One last question: when is the next lesson? . ⁧الدَّرْسُ القَادِمُ غَدًا مَسَاءً⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ Karīm: ad-darsu l-qādimu ġadan masāʾan. Karīm: The next lesson is tomorrow night. ! ⁧شُكْرًا يَا كَرِيمُ⁩ : ⁧مَارْيَا⁩ Māryā: šukran yā Karīm! Thank you. Karīm! What to notice. Each question begins with the question and then follows a normal nominal phrase: ⁧أَيْنَ⁩ + ⁧بَيْتُكَ⁩ , ⁧مَتَى⁩ + . ⁧الدَّرْسُ القَادِمُ⁩ The answer takes up the sentence without the question. ⁧عُمْر⁩ means age (Lett. title: Nationality and adjective of relation (nisba)
text: Lesson overview From ⁧مِصْر⁩ Egypt is formed ⁧مِصْرِيّ⁩ • Egyptian • Egyptian from ⁧عَرَب⁩ Arabic ⁧عَرَبِيّ⁩ (a) Arabic; from ⁧شُرْطَة⁩ Police ⁧شُرْطِيّ⁩ "Cop" is a cop. The suffix -iyy , called nisba () (the report) transforms a name into an adjective that indicates belonging. It is one of the most productive tools in Arabic: you will use it for nationality and languages, and then you will recognize it in hundreds of political, institutional and technical adjectives. Item Details Code A1-07 Level A1 · Module A1.2 "Ask and place" Prerequisites A1-06 exceeded Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 22 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-07), voice synthesis script, a map of the Arab world Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. to form the male and female nyba from the names of the main countries; 2. say and ask for nationality, provenance and residence; 3. Grant the nysba as an adjective ( ⁧رَجُلٌ مِصْرِيٌّ، الطَّالِبَةُ المِصْرِيَّةُ⁩ ); 4. appointing languages ( ⁧العَرَبِيَّةُ، الإِيطَالِيَّةُ⁩ …); 5. distinguish citizenship, ethnicity and language in presentations; 6. read educational charts and present people from different countries. Plan of the week. Dialogue 1 · At the coffee break of the conference Laylā, in Milan for a conference, knows other participants; Luca's with her. Laylā: Hi, I'm Laylā, Lebanese journalist. . ⁧أَنَا خَالِد، مِنَ العِرَاقِ⁩ . ⁧أَهْلًا⁩ : ⁧خَالِد⁩ Ḫālid: ahlan. anā Ḫālid, mina l-ʿIrāq. Khālid: Hello. I'm Khālid, from Iraq. ⁧هَلْ أَنْتَ عِرَاقِيٌّ مِنْ بَغْدَادَ؟⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ Laylā: hal door ʿirāqiyyun min Baġdād? Laylā: Are you an Iraqi from Baghdad? Rīm: No, I am Syrian of Aleppo, and alive (Lett. are resident) in Germany. ⁧وَمَنْ هُوَ؟⁩ : ⁧خَالِد⁩ Ḫālid: wa-man huwa? Khālid: Who is he? ⁧هُوَ لُوكَا، شُرْطِيٌّ إِيطَالِيٌّ،⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ ⁧وَهُوَ طَالِبٌ فِي صَفِّ اللُّغَةِ⁩ . ⁧العَرَبِيَّةِ⁩ Laylā: huwa Lūkā, šurṭiyyun īṭāliyyun, wa- huwa ṭālibun fī ṣaffi l-luġati l-ʿarabiyya. Laylā: He is Luca, an Italian policeman, and is a student in an Arabic language course. ⁧أَنَا إِيطَالِيٌّ مِنْ⁩ . ⁧أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: ahlan wa-sahlan. anā īṭāliyyun Min Luca: Pleasure. I'm Italian, from Milan. . ⁧مِيلَانُو⁩ Mīlānū. What to notice. Each nationality is an adjective in -iyy: ⁧لُبْنَانِيَّة⁩ , ⁧عِرَاقِيّ⁩ , ⁧سُورِيَّة⁩ , ⁧إِيطَالِيّ⁩ . It agrees with the person: Laylā è ⁧لُبْنَانِيَّة⁩ , Khālid ⁧مُقِيمَة⁩ . ⁧عِرَاقِيّ⁩ "resident" is the word of documents for "live" to... 2. How the Nisba Forms The basic rule has three steps: remove the article, remove the termination -a / -ā / -iyā name, add ⁧ـِيّ⁩ (male) or ⁧ـِيَّة⁩ (female). The nisba attaches itself to the root of the name: in ⁧سُورِيَا⁩ , ⁧إِيطَالِيَا⁩ , ⁧فَرَنْسَا⁩ the -iyā / -ā final is perceived as nonessential part and falls. In ⁧السُّعُودِيَّة⁩ the name of the country is already a female nyba (-[the kingdom] Saudi Arabia): removing the ⁧ة⁩ stays ⁧سُعُودِيّ⁩ . Not just countries. The same adjective form rule from any name: ⁧عَرَب⁩ → ⁧عَرَبِيّ⁩ "Arabic" is the word "Arabic"; ⁧دَوْلَة⁩ → ⁧دَوْلِيّ⁩ International (L0), ⁧سِيَاسَة⁩ → ⁧سِيَاسِيّ⁩ Politically speaking, this is the case (L0), ⁧شُرْطَة⁩ → ⁧شُرْطِيّ⁩ , ⁧أَمْن⁩ → ⁧أَمْنِيّ⁩ Safety-belted, ⁧رَسْم⁩ → ⁧رَسْمِيّ⁩ Official: Many adjectives of the print that you will read from B1 I'm Nisba. Cases to memorize. ⁧أَفْغَانِسْتَان⁩ → ⁧أَفْغَانِيّ⁩ (fall -istān), but ⁧بَاكِسْتَان⁩ → ⁧بَاكِسْتَانِيّ⁩ . The cities: ⁧بَغْدَاد⁩ → ⁧بَغْدَادِيّ⁩ , ⁧دِمَشْق⁩ → ⁧دِمَشْقِيّ⁩ , ⁧بَيْرُوت⁩ → ⁧بَيْرُوتِيّ⁩ . With plurals and other foreign names there are other exceptions: you will see them when they are needed. The pronunciation of -iyy. Inside the sentence the šadda You hear: miṣriyyun ; pause becomes ī long: miṣrī . To the female, the double always remains: miṣriyya . 3. The nyba as an adjective The nyba is an adjective like the others (A1-03, A1-04): follows the name and generally agrees and determination. She's Egyptian. ⁧طَبِيبٌ سُورِيٌّ⁩ ṭabībun sūrī a Syrian doctor ⁧الصَّحَفِيَّةُ اللُّبْنَانِيَّةُ⁩ aṣ-ṣaḥafiyyatu l-lubnāniyya the Lebanese journalist . ⁧المُتَرْجِمُ المَغْرِبِيُّ مَشْهُورٌ⁩ al-mutarǧimu l-maġribiyyu mašhūr. The Moroccan interpreter is famous. ⁧الحُكُومَةُ العِرَاقِيَّةُ⁩ al-ḥukūmatu l-ʿirāqiyya the Iraqi Government Nationality as predicate: without article. "I am Egyptian" = ⁧أَنَا مِصْرِيٌّ⁩ . ⁧أَنَا المِصْرِيُّ⁩ I am the Egyptian (of which we speak) A1-02. With the institutions. The government, the ministry, the army of a country are indicated with the nysba: ⁧الجَيْشُ اللُّبْنَانِيُّ⁩ The Lebanese army shall be: ⁧وِزَارَةُ الدَّاخِلِيَّةِ المِصْرِيَّةُ⁩ The Ministry of the Interior of Egypt. For now: ⁧لُغَتِي⁩ My language is... ⁧أَنَا طَالِبٌ فِي صَفِّ العَرَبِيَّةِ⁩ I am a student in the Arabic course. 5. Citizenship, ethnicity, language In documents, citizenship is ⁧الجِنْسِيَّة⁩ al-ǧinsiyya : ⁧الجِنْسِيَّةُ⁩ : . ⁧مِصْرِيَّةٌ⁩ It does not always coincide with the belonging of a person or his language: • an Iraqi or Syrian citizen may be Arabic ( ⁧عَرَبِيّ⁩ ) or Kurdish ( ⁧كُرْدِيّ⁩ ), and have as first language Arabic or Kurdish; • a Moroccan or Algerian citizen may be Arabic or Amazigh ( ⁧أَمَازِيغِيّ⁩ ), and speak Arabic, a language amazigh or both; • ⁧عَرَبِيّ⁩ indicates membership of Arabic language and culture, not citizenship. In professional communication, you use the term that the person uses for himself and, in documents, always distinguish the three data. Confounding them is one of the most common mistakes in journalistic descriptions. 6. Pronunciation The doubles of the nyba. Inside the sentence: ʿirāqiyyun min Baġdād , šurṭiyyun īṭāliyy(one) . Pause: ʿirāqī , īṭālī . To the female always -iyya . ⁧ع⁩ and ⁧ق⁩ in ⁧عِرَاقِيّ⁩ . One ʿayn at the beginning and one qāf in the center: two sounds absent in English in the same word. Irāki with k is the Italian pronunciation to be avoided. ⁧ص⁩ in ⁧البَصْرَة⁩ , ⁧ح⁩ in ⁧حَلَب⁩ . Basra begins with the article and a ṣād Emphasis: al-Baṣra . Aleppo is ⁧حَلَب⁩ Ḥalab , ḥāʾ. Names of foreign countries. ⁧إِيطَالِيَا⁩ , ⁧أَلْمَانِيَا⁩ , ⁧فَرَنْسَا⁩ long vowels are written (ī, ā) and must be kept. 7. Notes of use. The plural of the nysba in person is often regular (-iyyūn), but some have their own pluralities: ⁧مَغَارِبَة⁩ Moroccans (including Moroccans) ⁧عَرَب⁩ "Arabic" is equal to or greater than "Arabic"; ⁧أَكْرَاد⁩ "Kurdish." ⁧بَلَد⁩ means country, country, country, in Egypt and the Levant ⁧بَلَد⁩ It is also used for Christmas cities. ⁧مُقِيم⁩ is the word of documents: ⁧الإِقَامَة⁩ al-iqāma is the residence permit (s) or residence (s). 8. title: Prepositions and expression of having
text: Lesson overview Arabic does not have a verb "to have" . To say "I have a machine" says "I have a machine": ⁧عِنْدِي⁩ . ⁧سَيَّارَةٌ⁩ This unit gives you the prepositions to place people and objects in space (above, below, in front, next to) and the three buildings of possession with ⁧عِنْدَ⁩ , ⁧لِـ⁩ and ⁧مَعَ⁩ . You will also learn that after a preposition the name changes the final vowel: it is the first grammatical case you consciously use. Two weeks. Item Details Code A1-08 Level A1 · Module A1.2 "Ask and place" Prerequisites A1-07 exceeded Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 23–24 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-08), voice synthesis script, a plan of your room designed by hand, session with the tutor in the second week Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. use the most frequent site prepositions and tell where objects and people are located; 2. put the name to the genitive after a preposition ( ⁧فِي البَيْتِ، فِي بَيْتٍ كَبِيرٍ⁩ ); 3. attach singular suffix pronouns to prepositions ( ⁧عِنْدِي، مَعَكَ، لَهَا، فِيهِ⁩ ); 4. express possession with ⁧عِنْدَ⁩ , ⁧لِـ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ⁩ and deny it with ⁧لَيْسَ عِنْدِي⁩ ; 5. give simple directions in the city without verbs; 6. describe a room and write what you possess in 40 words. Two-week plan. Dialogue 1 · Where is the key? In the office, Luca looks for the key to the archive. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧أَيْنَ المِفْتَاحُ يَا كَرِيمُ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: ayna l-miftāḥu yā Karīm? Luke: Where is the key, Karīm? ⁧عَلَى المَكْتَبِ، بِجَانِبِ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ . ⁧الحَاسُوبِ⁩ Karīm: ʿalā l-maktabi, bi-ǧānibi l-ḥāsūb. Karīm: On the desk, next to the computer. ⁧لَا، عَلَى المَكْتَبِ أَوْرَاقٌ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ . ⁧فَقَطْ⁩ Lūkā: lā, ʿalā l-maktabi awrāqun faqaṭ. No, there's only paper on the desk. ⁧هَلِ المِفْتَاحُ فِي الحَقِيبَةِ؟⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ Karīm: hali l-miftāḥu fī l-ḥaqība? Karīm: Is the key in the bag? ⁧الحَقِيبَةُ تَحْتَ الطَّاوِلَةِ،⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧وَفِيهَا جَوَازُ سَفَرِي وَهَاتِفِي⁩ . ⁧فَقَطْ⁩ Lūkā: al-ḥaqībatu taḥta ṭ-ṭāwila, wa- fīhā ǧawāzu safarī wa-hātifī faqaṭ. Luca: The bag is under the table, and inside there are only my passport and my phone. ⁧المِفْتَاحُ مَعِي،⁩ ! ⁧آه، آسِف⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ! ⁧فِي جَيْبِي⁩ Karīm: āh, āsif! al-miftāḥu maʿī, fī ǧaybī! Karīm: Sorry! I have the key in my pocket! ! ⁧الحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: al-ḥamdu li-llāh! Luca: Thank God! What to notice. After each preposition the name ends in -i: ⁧عَلَى المَكْتَبِ⁩ , ⁧بِجَانِبِ الحَاسُوبِ⁩ , ⁧تَحْتَ فِيهَا⁩ . ⁧الطَّاوِلَةِ⁩ It shall be ⁧فِي⁩ with the suffix -hā (The bag is feminine). ⁧مَعِي⁩ With me, he expresses what is on him at that moment. ⁧الحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ⁩ here it's worth less bad. 2. Prepositions of place Preposition Meaning Example ⁧فِي⁩ fī in, in ⁧فِي الغُرْفَةِ⁩ In the room ⁧عَلَى⁩ ʿalā Up, above (contact) ⁧عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ⁩ On the table ⁧فَوْقَ⁩ fawqa above (without contact) ⁧فَوْقَ المَكْتَبِ⁩ Over the desk. ⁧تَحْتَ⁩ taḥta below ⁧تَحْتَ السَّرِيرِ⁩ Under the bed ⁧أَمَامَ⁩ amāma before ⁧أَمَامَ البَابِ⁩ In front of the door ⁧خَلْفَ⁩ ḫalfa behind ⁧خَلْفَ البَيْتِ⁩ behind the house ⁧بِجَانِبِ⁩ bi-ǧānibi next to ⁧بِجَانِبِ النَّافِذَةِ⁩ • next to the window • ⁧بَيْنَ⁩ bayna between ⁧بَيْنَ البَنْكِ وَالمَطْعَمِ⁩ The bank and the restaurant are located between the bank and the restaurant ⁧عِنْدَ⁩ ʿinda near, from (to) ⁧عِنْدَ الطَّبِيبِ⁩ From the doctor ⁧مِنْ⁩ min from ⁧مِنَ المَكْتَبِ⁩ From the office ⁧إِلَى⁩ ilā in, to ⁧إِلَى المَحَطَّةِ⁩ At the station ⁧مَعَ⁩ maʿa with ⁧مَعَ صَدِيقِي⁩ With my friend ⁧لِـ⁩ li- for, a; of (membership) ⁧لِلطَّالِبِ⁩ For the student: ⁧بِـ⁩ bi- with (instrument), in, by means of ⁧بِالسَّيَّارَةِ⁩ In the machine ⁧عَنْ⁩ ʿan regarding, on; from (far from) ⁧عَنِ المَدِينَةِ⁩ The city is under attack. ⁧لِـ⁩ and ⁧بِـ⁩ , as ⁧وَ⁩ ( L0-10): ⁧لِلطَّالِبِ⁩ , ⁧بِالسَّيَّارَةِ⁩ . With the article ⁧لِـ⁩ loses the alif: . ⁧لِلْ⁩ Preposition-name. ⁧فَوْقَ⁩ , ⁧تَحْتَ⁩ , ⁧أَمَامَ⁩ , ⁧خَلْفَ⁩ , ⁧بَيْنَ⁩ , ⁧عِنْدَ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ⁩ They end up in -a: originally they are names to the accusative used as place adverbs. For this reason the name that follows you is a complement of specification, to the genitive, as in aiḍāfa (A1-10). 3. The genitive after the preposition After any preposition the name is at the genitive ( ⁧مَجْرُور⁩ maǧrūr , "Draged"): desinence becomes -i if the name is determined, -indeterminate. The adjective that follows it agrees also in case. Normal case (nominative) After preposition (genital) Transliteration  ⁧فِي البَيْتِ الكَبِيرِالبَيْتُ الكَبِيرُ⁩ fī l-bayti l-kabīr  ⁧فِي بَيْتٍ كَبِيرٍبَيْتٌ كَبِيرٌ⁩ fī baytin kabīr  ⁧مِنَ الغُرْفَةِ الصَّغِيرَةِالغُرْفَةُ الصَّغِيرَةُ⁩ mina l-ġurfati ṣ-ṣaġīra  ⁧فِي مَدِينَةٍ قَدِيمَةٍمَدِينَةٌ قَدِيمَةٌ⁩ fī madīnatin qadīma ⁧فِي بَغْدَادَ، مِنْ مِصْرَبَغْدَادُ، مِصْرُ⁩ fī Baġdādmin Miṣr The diptotic names (many proper names, some plurals) to the indeterminate genitive take -a, without tanwīn: ⁧فِي بَغْدَادَ⁩ , ⁧مِنْ لُبْنَانَ⁩ , ⁧مِنْ أَطِبَّاءَ⁩ . You've met them before: now you know why. In pause desinence falls, as always: fī I-bayt. But inside the sentence it must be read, and in the vocally written texts you see it written: it is proof that a name depends on a preposition. Because you need it. title: The singular suffix pronouns on names
text: Lesson overview My book is a suffix attached to the name. You've known him since ⁧اِسْمِي⁩ , ⁧حَالُكَ⁩ , ⁧عِنْدَهُ⁩ ; Now you study it systematically, with its rules of handwriting and pronunciation, and use it to talk about the family. You will also learn the words of kinship, including the distinction between paternal and maternal uncles that Italian does not make. Item Details Code A1-09 Level A1 · Module A1.2 "Ask and place" Prerequisites A1-08 exceeded Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 25 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-09), script for speech synthesis, family photos (your or invented) Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. attack the suffixes -ī, -ka, -ki, -hu, -hā in any name, even with ⁧ة⁩ ; 2. use the case vowel before the suffix and pass -hu → -hi; 3. accord the adjective with a name with a suffix ( ⁧بَيْتُهُ الكَبِيرُ⁩ ); 4. use special forms of ⁧أَب⁩ and ⁧أَخ⁩ ; 5. appoint family members and describe a family tree; 6. Talk about your family for a minute. Plan of the week. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · section 1: the family suffix table · vocabulary 2 Sections 2–3: ⁧ة⁩ → ⁧ت⁩ , the vowel before the suffix, -hi · exercises 1–3 3 Section 4: ⁧أَب⁩ and ⁧أَخ⁩ · section 5: names and kinship · exercises 4–5 4 Pronunciation · examples in context · exercise 6 5 Reading: the family tree · exercise 7 6 Writing · listening · oral production with the tutor 7 Unit verification · review Anki 1. Dialogue 1 · The family of Karīm Karīm Show Luca a picture taken in Fes. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧هَلْ هٰذِهِ عَائِلَتُكَ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: hal hāḏihi ʿāʾilatuka? Is this your family? ⁧هٰذَا أَبِي، وَهٰذِهِ⁩ . ⁧نَعَمْ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧أَبِي مُدَرِّسٌ، وَأُمِّي⁩ . ⁧أُمِّي⁩ . ⁧طَبِيبَةٌ⁩ Karīm: naʿam. hāḏā abī, wa-hāḏihi ummī. abī mudarrisun, wa-ummī ṭabība. Karīm: Yes. This is my father and this is my mother. My father is a teacher and my mother is a doctor. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧وَمَنْ هٰذَا الشَّابُّ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-man hāḏā š-šābb? Luca: And who is this boy? ⁧هٰذَا أَخِي الصَّغِيرُ، اسْمُهُ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ . ⁧هُوَ طَالِبٌ فِي الرِّبَاطِ⁩ . ⁧يَاسِين⁩ Karīm: hāḏā aḫī ṣ-ṣaġīr, ismuhu Yāsīn. huwa ṭālibun fī r-Ribāṭ. Karīm: He is my younger brother, his name Yāsīn. He's a student in Rabat. ⁧وَهٰذِهِ المَرْأَةُ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-hāḏihi l-marʾa? What about this woman? ⁧هِيَ أُخْتِي سُعَاد، مَعَ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ . ⁧زَوْجِهَا وَابْنِهَا⁩ Karīm: hiya uḫtī Suʿād, maʿa zawǧihā wa- bnihā. Karīm: She's my sister Suʿād, with her husband and son. ⁧عَائِلَتُكَ⁩ ! ⁧مَا شَاءَ اللهُ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ . ⁧كَبِيرَةٌ⁩ Lūkā: mā šāʾa llāh! ʿāʾilatuka kabīra. Luca: That's nice! Your family is large. ⁧وَأَنْتَ؟ هَلْ⁩ . ⁧الحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧لَكَ إِخْوَةٌ؟⁩ Karīm: al-ḥamdu li-llāh. wa-anta? hal laka iḫwa? Karīm: Thank God. What about you? Do you have any brothers? ⁧لِي أُخْتٌ وَاحِدَةٌ، اسْمُهَا⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧هِيَ مُتَزَوِّجَةٌ، وَزَوْجُهَا⁩ . ⁧جُولْيَا⁩ . ⁧مُهَنْدِسٌ⁩ Lūkā: lī uḫtun wāḥidatun, ismuhā Ǧūlyā. hiya mutazawwiǧatun, wa-zawǧuhā muhandis. I only have one sister, her name is Giulia. She's married and her husband is an engineer. ⁧وَأَنْتَ؟ هَلْ أَنْتَ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧مُتَزَوِّجٌ؟⁩ Karīm: wa-anta? hal anta mutazawwiǧ? Karīm: What about you? Are you married? . ⁧لَا، أَنَا أَعْزَبُ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: lā, anā aʿzab. No, they're single. What to notice. ⁧اسْمُهُ⁩ His name is his, ⁧اسْمُهَا⁩ The same word with two suffixes. After ⁧مَعَ⁩ the name with suffix is to the genitive: . ⁧مَعَ زَوْجِهَا⁩ In ⁧وَابْنِهَا⁩ the alif ⁧اِبْن⁩ è waṣla: wa-bnihā . ⁧أَخِي الصَّغِيرُ⁩ My younger brother has the adjective with the article, because the name with suffix is determined (A1-04). 2. The singular suffix table Person Suffix ⁧كِتَاب⁩ Book of books ⁧سَيَّارَة⁩ • auto-crystal Translation me ⁧ـِي⁩ -ī ⁧كِتَابِي⁩ kitābī ⁧سَيَّارَتِي⁩ sayyāratī my book, my car you (m.) ⁧ـكَ⁩ -ka ⁧كِتَابُكَ⁩ kitābuka ⁧سَيَّارَتُكَ⁩ sayyāratuka Your... you (f.) ⁧ـكِ⁩ -ki ⁧كِتَابُكِ⁩ kitābuki ⁧سَيَّارَتُكِ⁩ sayyāratuki Your... (to a woman) him ⁧ـهُ⁩ -hu ⁧كِتَابُهُ⁩ kitābuhu ⁧سَيَّارَتُهُ⁩ sayyāratuhu his... (of him) She ⁧ـهَا⁩ -hā ⁧كِتَابُهَا⁩ kitābuhā ⁧سَيَّارَتُهَا⁩ sayyāratuhā your... (of her) The suffix indicates the owner, not the possessed thing. In Italian  "his" does not say whether the owner is a man or a woman; in Arabic yes: ⁧كِتَابُهُ⁩ is the book of him, ⁧كِتَابُهَا⁩ The book of her. The kind of book doesn't count. The name with suffix is determined: no article, nothing tanwīn (A1-04). 3. Three rules of form 1) ⁧ة⁩ becomes ⁧ت⁩ . In front of any suffix tāʾ marbūṭa opens in tāʾ: ⁧سَيَّارَة⁩ → ⁧سَيَّارَتِي⁩ , ⁧مَدِينَة⁩ → ⁧مَدِينَتُهَا⁩ , ⁧عَائِلَة⁩ → ⁧عَائِلَتُكَ⁩ . It is always pronounced t . 2) The vowel of the case is before the suffix. The name holds his desinence: -u to the name, -a to the accused, - I'm in the genitive. In front of the suffix there is no tanwīn. Name Genitive (after preposition) Translation . ⁧فِي بَيْتِكَبَيْتُكَ كَبِيرٌ⁩ Your house is big. · in your home . ⁧سَيَّارَتُهَا جَدِيدَةٌ⁩ ⁧فِي سَيَّارَتِهَا⁩ Your car is new. · in your car With -ī The voice of the case is not heard: ⁧كِتَابِي⁩ It's the same in all cases. 3) -hu becomes -hi after i, ī or ay, so also to the genitive: ⁧فِي بَيْتِهِ⁩ fī baytihi ... in his house... ⁧مَعَ أَخِيهِ⁩ With her Brother ⁧عَلَيْهِ⁩ On him. The pronunciation follows the previous vowel: it is a vocal harmony, not a different case. The adjective after a name with suffix takes the article and case of the name: ⁧بَيْتُهُ الجَدِيدُ⁩ His new house is in the middle of the world. ⁧فِي بَيْتِهِ الجَدِيدِ⁩ In his new house. Without an article it becomes preached: ⁧بَيْتُهُ جَدِيدٌ⁩ His house is new. 4. ⁧أَب⁩ and ⁧أَخ⁩ : special forms "Father" and "brother" when they have a suffix (other than -ī) or another name later, lengthen the appropriate vowel:  me you (m.) him She Name ⁧أَبِي⁩ abī ⁧أَبُوكَ⁩ abūka ⁧أَبُوهُ⁩ abūhu ⁧أَبُوهَا⁩ abūhā Genitive  ⁧أَبِيكَأَبِي⁩ abīka ⁧أَبِيهِ⁩ abīhi ⁧أَبِيهَا⁩ abīhā Accused ⁧أَبَاكَأَبِي⁩ abāka ⁧أَبَاهُ⁩ abāhu ⁧أَبَاهَا⁩ abāhā ⁧أَخ⁩ It works the same way: ⁧أَخِي⁩ , ⁧أَخُوكَ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ أَخِيهِ⁩ . Even in front of a name: ⁧أَخُو أَبِي⁩ "My father's brother" ⁧فِي بَيْتِ أَبِي سَلْمَى⁩ At the home of the father of Salmā». In practice. For A1 use safely ⁧أَبِي⁩ / ⁧أَخِي⁩ and the shape of the name ( ⁧أَبُوكَ⁩ , ⁧أَخُوهُ⁩ ); the others recognize them. In standard Arabic they are often used also ⁧وَالِد⁩ wālid "Father" ⁧وَالِدَة⁩ wālida "Mother' is the name of the family. ⁧الوَالِدَانِ⁩ The parents who have regular forms: ⁧وَالِدُكَ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ وَالِدِهِ⁩ . 5. The family and names Arabic Transliteration Meaning Note ⁧جَدَّة⁩ / ⁧جَدّ⁩ ǧadd / ǧadda Grandpa / Grandma  ⁧أُمّ⁩ / ⁧أَب⁩ ab / umm father / mother  ⁧بِنْت⁩ , ⁧اِبْنَة⁩ / ⁧اِبْن⁩ ibn / ibna, bint child / daughter ⁧بِنْت⁩ is more common ⁧أُخْت⁩ / ⁧أَخ⁩ aḫ / uḫt brother/sister  ⁧زَوْجَة⁩ / ⁧زَوْج⁩ zawǧ / zawǧa husband / wife  ⁧عَمَّة⁩ / ⁧عَمّ⁩ ʿamm / ʿamma Uncle / paternal aunt brother / sister of father ⁧خَالَة⁩ / ⁧خَال⁩ ḫāl / ḫāla Uncle / Aunt Materni brother/sister of mother ⁧اِبْنُ العَمِّ⁩ ibnu l-ʿamm cousin (son of father's uncle) and so ⁧بِنْتُ الخَالِ⁩ etc. Because two "zii" are. In traditional Arabic societies, the father's and mother's families have different roles, and the language always distinguishes them. In a conversation, my uncle requires a choice: ⁧عَمِّي⁩ or ⁧خَالِي⁩ . Names in person. In the chain of the name, "son" is written without aliph between two names: ⁧مُحَمَّد بْن عَلِيّ⁩ Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī (you often read bin). Many adults are called with the kunya, the father of / mother of the child + the name of the first child: ⁧أَبُو أَحْمَد⁩ Abū Aḥmad , ⁧أُمُّ يُوسُف⁩ Umm Yūsuf . It is a loving and respectful use. The complete structure of the Arabic name (ism, nasab, kunya, laqab, nisba) you will study it in A2. 6. Pronunciation -ka, -ki, -hu, -hā They don't eat. In the pause, the disappearance of the case falls, but the suffix remains whole: kitābuka , kitābuki . In the quick talk and dialects they become -ak , -ik , -u , -ha: recognize them, but in full pronunciation MSA. The t of ⁧ة⁩ . sayyāratī , madīnatuhā : the t is clearly heard. ⁧ع⁩ in ⁧عَمّ⁩ , ⁧خ⁩ in ⁧خَال⁩ . ʿamm (ʿayn + double m) and ḫāl (ḫāʾ scraped): two sounds that distinguish two relatives. The šadda. ⁧جَدّ⁩ ǧadd , ⁧عَمّ⁩ ʿamm , ⁧أُمّ⁩ umm: the final double consonant can be heard especially with the suffix: ⁧جَدِّي⁩ ǧaddī , ⁧عَمِّي⁩ ʿammī , ⁧أُمِّي⁩ ummī . 7. Reading · The family tree of Salmā ⁧لِي أَخٌ وَاحِدٌ،⁩ . ⁧أُمِّي اسْمُهَا نَوَال، وَهِيَ مُدَرِّسَةٌ⁩ . ⁧أَبِي اسْمُهُ حَسَن، وَهُوَ مُهَنْدِسٌ⁩ . ⁧هٰذِهِ عَائِلَتِي⁩ ⁧بِنْتِي⁩ . ⁧زَوْجِي اسْمُهُ عَادِل، وَهُوَ طَبِيبٌ فِي مِيلَانُو⁩ . ⁧اسْمُهُ طَارِق، وَهُوَ طَالِبٌ فِي الجَامِعَةِ⁩ ⁧خَالَتِي⁩ . ⁧عَمِّي أَحْمَد هُوَ أَخُو أَبِي، وَهُوَ مُقِيمٌ فِي الإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّةِ⁩ . ⁧اسْمُهَا نُور، وَهِيَ صَغِيرَةٌ جِدًّا⁩ ⁧جَدَّتِي امْرَأَةٌ قَوِيَّةٌ، وَهِيَ⁩ . ⁧سُهَى هِيَ أُخْتُ أُمِّي، وَبَيْتُهَا قَرِيبٌ مِنْ بَيْتِ جَدَّتِي فِي القَاهِرَةِ⁩ . ⁧حَبِيبَةُ العَائِلَةِ كُلِّهَا⁩ Glossary: ⁧الإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّة⁩ al-Iskandariyya ... Listening Script A · Dialog 1 ⁧وَمَنْ هٰذَا الشَّابُّ؟ هٰذَا⁩ . ⁧أَبِي مُدَرِّسٌ، وَأُمِّي طَبِيبَةٌ⁩ . ⁧هٰذَا أَبِي، وَهٰذِهِ أُمِّي⁩ . ⁧هَلْ هٰذِهِ عَائِلَتُكَ؟ نَعَمْ⁩ ⁧وَهٰذِهِ المَرْأَةُ؟ هِيَ أُخْتِي سُعَاد، مَعَ زَوْجِهَا⁩ . ⁧هُوَ طَالِبٌ فِي الرِّبَاطِ⁩ . ⁧أَخِي الصَّغِيرُ، اسْمُهُ يَاسِين⁩ . ⁧وَابْنِهَا⁩ Script B · The family of Hudā ⁧زَوْجُهَا⁩ . ⁧لِي أُخْتٌ كَبِيرَةٌ، اسْمُهَا مَرْيَم، وَهِيَ مُتَزَوِّجَةٌ⁩ . ⁧أَبِي تُونِسِيٌّ، وَأُمِّي إِيطَالِيَّةٌ⁩ . ⁧اِسْمِي هُدَى⁩ ⁧جَدِّي، أَبُو أَبِي، كَبِيرٌ فِي السِّنِّ، وَهُوَ فِي⁩ . ⁧خَالِي فِي رُومَا، وَعَمِّي فِي تُونِسَ⁩ . ⁧مِصْرِيٌّ، وَهُوَ صَحَفِيٌّ⁩ . ⁧بَيْتِ عَمِّي⁩ 13. Oral production 1. Family photos. Show the tutor a photo (or drawing) and present five people: ⁧هٰذَا أَخِي، اسْمُهُ⁩ … 2. Questions. The tutor asks you: ⁧مَا اسْمُ أَبِيكَ؟ هَلْ لَكَ إِخْوَةٌ؟ أَيْنَ بَيْتُ عَمِّكَ؟⁩ Answer with full sentences, Then you ask the tutor the same questions. 3. One minute. Talk about your family for a minute without reading. Sign up. 14. Typical errors Error Correction ⁧سَيَّارَتِيمَدِينَةُهَا⁩ , ⁧سَيَّارَةِي⁩ , ⁧مَدِينَتُهَا⁩ : ⁧ة⁩ becomes ⁧ت⁩ ⁧الكِتَابُهُ⁩ : ⁧كِتَابُهُ⁩ suffix and article are excluded ⁧فِي بَيْتِهُ⁩ : ⁧فِي بَيْتِهِ⁩ -hu becomes -hi after the Choose -hu/-hā according to the kind of thing The holder shall count: ⁧كِتَابُهَا⁩ = the book of her ⁧بَيْتُهُ كَبِيرٌ⁩ for his great house ⁧بَيْتُهُ الكَبِيرُ⁩ (syntagma); ⁧بَيْتُهُ كَبِيرٌ⁩ = "His house is great" ⁧أَبِيكَ مُهَنْدِسٌ⁩ : ⁧أَبُوكَ مُهَنْدِسٌ⁩ subject to name My uncle always ⁧عَمِّيعَمِّي⁩ (paternal) or ⁧خَالِي⁩ (mother) kitābak , kitābu in MSA kitābuka , kitābuhu 15. Flashcard Deck A1, tag A1-09: 23 rumors. ( ⁧وَاحِد⁩ "One" is in the deck with numbers, A1-11.) For each kinship word say also the form with -ī ( ⁧أُمِّي، عَمِّي⁩ ...) and with -hu. 16. title: L'iḍāfa simple
text: Lesson overview ⁧وِزَارَةُ الدَّاخِلِيَّةِ⁩ The Ministry of the Interior, ⁧جَامِعَةُ القَاهِرَةِ⁩ The University of Cairo, ⁧مَكْتَبُ المُدِيرِ⁩ The Director's office is: two names placed one after the other, without preposition, express our . È l' iḍāfa ( ⁧إِضَافَة⁩ , () annexation), the building that bears almost all the names of institutions, offices and places. Without iḍāfa You don't read a newspaper headline. In this unity you learn it, distinguish it from the name with adjective and use it with the basic institutional vocabulary. Two weeks; close the form A1.2. Item Details Code A1-10 Level A1 · Module A1.2 "Ask and place" Prerequisites A1-09 exceeded Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 26–27 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-10), voice synthesis script, tutor session in the second week Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. form theiḍāfa: first term without article and without tanwīn, second term to the genitive; 2. read the ⁧ة⁩ the first term as -at; 3. to understand when aiḍāfa is determined or indeterminate; 4. add an adjective to aiḍāfa and understand what name it refers to; 5. distinguish iḍāfa and name + adjective ( ⁧جَامِعَةُ القَاهِرَةِ⁩ / ⁧المَتْحَفُ المِصْرِيُّ⁩ ), even without vowels; 6. read signs, headers and short news with names of institutions and summarize them in three sentences. Two-week plan. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · section 1: how to form theiḍāfa 2 Section 2: the pronunciation of the first term · exercises 1–2 3 Section 3: determined or indefinite · year 3 4 Section 4: iḍāfa or adjective? · year 4 5 Pronunciation · lexicon (first half) · insignia 6 Listening: script B · exercise 10 7 Review Anki 8 Section 5: chains · section 6: iḍāfa and adjective · exercises 5–6 9 Section 7: institutions and offices · vocabulary (second half) · exercise 7 10 Reading: didactic news, with and without vowels · exercise 8 11 Writing: summarized in three sentences 12 Session with the tutor · listening to the news 13 Unit verification 14 Module Review A1.2 for the test 1. Dialogue 1 · The insignia of Cairo Salmā show Luca some pictures taken in Cairo. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧مَا هٰذِهِ الصُّورَةُ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: mā hāḏihi ṣ-ṣūra? Luca: What photo is this? ⁧هٰذِهِ صُورَةُ شَارِعٍ فِي⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ . ⁧هٰذَا شَارِعُ التَّحْرِيرِ⁩ . ⁧القَاهِرَةِ⁩ Salmā: hāḏihi ṣūratu šāriʿin fī l-Qāhira. hāḏā šāriʿu t-taḥrīr. Salmā: This is a photo of a street in Cairo. That's it. Taḥrīr. ⁧وَهٰذَا المَبْنَى الكَبِيرُ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-hāḏā l-mabnā l-kabīr? Luca: What about this big building? ⁧هِيَ⁩ . ⁧هٰذِهِ جَامِعَةُ القَاهِرَةِ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ . ⁧جَامِعَةٌ قَدِيمَةٌ وَمَشْهُورَةٌ⁩ Salmā: hāḏihi ǧāmiʿatu l-Qāhira. hiya ǧāmiʿatun qadīmatun wa-mašhūra. Salmā: It is the University of Cairo. It is an ancient and famous university. ⁧قِسْمُ⁩ » ⁧وَعَلَى تِلْكَ اللَّافِتَةِ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧؟⁩ « ⁧قِسْم⁩ » ⁧مَا مَعْنَى⁩ .« ⁧الشُّرْطَةِ⁩ Lūkā: wa-ʿalā tilka l-lāfitati «qismu š- šurṭa». mā maʿnā «qism»? Luke: And on that sign there is a- šurṭa». What does "qism" mean? ⁧، لٰكِنْ⁩ « ⁧جُزْء⁩ » ⁧مَعْنَاهُ⁩ « ⁧قِسْم⁩ » : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧فِي مِصْرَ قِسْمُ الشُّرْطَةِ هُوَ مَرْكَزُ⁩ . ⁧الشُّرْطَةِ⁩ Salmā: «qism» maʿnāhu «ǧuzʾ», lākin fī Miṣra qismu š-šurṭati huwa markazu š- šurṭa. Salmā: "Qism" means "part," "section" but in Egypt, "qism" means "part" al-šurṭa It's the police station. ⁧؟ هَلْ⁩ « ⁧المَتْحَفُ المِصْرِيُّ⁩ » ⁧وَ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧هٰذِهِ إِضَافَةٌ أَيْضًا؟⁩ Lūkā: wa-«al-matḥafu l-miṣrī»? hal hāḏihi iḍāfatun ayḍan? Luke: Andal-matḥaf al-miṣrī»? It's a...iḍāfa This one too? « ⁧المَتْحَفُ المِصْرِيُّ⁩ » ! ⁧لَا⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ . ⁧اسْمٌ وَصِفَةٌ⁩ Salmā: lā! «al-matḥafu l-miṣrī» ismun wa-ṣifa. Salmā: No! The Egyptian Museum is a name with an adjective. What to notice. In ⁧جَامِعَةُ القَاهِرَةِ⁩ and ⁧شَارِعُ التَّحْرِيرِ⁩ the first name does not have the article, the second yes: it is a 'iḍāfa. In ⁧المَتْحَفُ المِصْرِيُّ⁩ both have the article: it's an adjective name (A1-04). ⁧مَعْنَى⁩ • Meaning: ⁧مَعْنَاهُ⁩ Its meaning is used to ask for the meaning of a word: ⁧مَا مَعْنَى⁩ … ⁧؟⁩ 2. How to form theiḍāfa First term ( ⁧مُضَاف⁩ muḍāf ) Second term ( ⁧مُضَاف إِلَيْهِ⁩ muḍāf layhi) Together Translation  ⁧بَابُ البَيْتِالبَيْتبَاب⁩ bābu l-bayt the door of the house ⁧مَدِينَة⁩  ⁧مَدِينَةُ مِيلَانُومِيلَانُو⁩ madīnatu Mīlānū the city of Milan ⁧مَكْتَب⁩  ⁧مَكْتَبُ المُدِيرِالمُدِير⁩ maktabu l- mudīr the Director's office  ⁧وِزَارَةُ الدَّاخِلِيَّةِالدَّاخِلِيَّةوِزَارَة⁩ wizāratu d- dāḫiliyya the Ministry of the Interior ⁧سَيَّارَةُ أَخِيأَخِيسَيَّارَة⁩ sayyāratu aḫī my brother's car The three rules. 1. The first term has no article or tanwīn. It is determined by the second, as the name with suffix: door of the house is said to be "porta la-casa" . 2. The second term is to the genitive: -i if determined, -indeterminately, -a for diptotes without article ( ⁧سَفِيرُ تُونِسَ⁩ ). 3. The first term takes the case required by the sentence: subject -u ( ⁧بَابُ البَيْتِ كَبِيرٌ⁩ ), after preposition -i ( ⁧أَمَامَ بَابِ البَيْتِ⁩ ). Because that's how it works. L'iḍāfa It's like a name with a suffix, but instead of the suffix there's another name: ⁧كِتَابُهُ⁩ His book is → ⁧كِتَابُ الطَّالِبِ⁩ The student's book is the same as the student's. For this reason, the first name cannot have the article: it is already possessed. 3. The pronunciation of the first term The ⁧ة⁩ read -at. In the first term, ⁧ة⁩ it is always followed by desinence and the middle name: madīnatu Mīlānū , wizāratu d-dāḫiliyya , ǧāmiʿatu l-Qāhira . Even in the speech without termination, t remains: wizārat ad- dāḫiliyya , ǧāmiʿat al-Qāhira . It's the safest way to recognize aiḍāfa I'm listening. The ligament. The termination of the first term is linked to the article of the second: bābu l-bayt, maktabu l-mudīr . With solar letters: šāriʿu t-taḥrīr , qismu š-šurṭa . 4. Determined or indefinite Iḍāfa Second term Translation ⁧بَابُ البَيْتِ⁩ determined the door of the house ⁧بَابُ بَيْتٍ⁩ indeterminate a door to a house ⁧كِتَابُ الطَّالِبِ⁩ determined the student book ⁧كِتَابُ طَالِبٍ⁩ indeterminate the book of a student ⁧صُورَةُ شَارِعٍ⁩ undetermined a photo of a street L'iḍāfa the whole takes the determination of the second term. With a proper name or suffix it is determined: ⁧سَفِيرُ تُونِسَ⁩ The Ambassador of Tunisia is hereby appointed as Head of Mission of the Republic of Tunisia. ⁧بَيْتُ أَبِي⁩ It's my father's house. 5. Iḍāfa or name with adjective? Structure Example Translation How to recognize it Iḍāfa ⁧جَامِعَةُ القَاهِرَةِ⁩ University of Cairo first name without article Name + adjective ⁧الجَامِعَةُ الأَمْرِيكِيَّةُ⁩ American University both with the article Iḍāfa ⁧وِزَارَةُ الخَارِجِيَّةِ⁩ the Ministry of Foreign Affairs first without article Name + adjective ⁧الوِزَارَةُ الجَدِيدَةُ⁩ the new ministry both with the article No vowels. : ⁧جامعة القاهرة⁩ first word without ⁧الـ⁩ , second with ⁧الـ⁩ → iḍāfa. : ⁧الجامعة الأمريكية⁩ two articles → name + adjective. It is the first analysis to be done on each title. Warning to ⁧الدَّاخِلِيَّة⁩ and ⁧الخَارِجِيَّة⁩ . They are women's nisba used as names: "internal affairs," "external affairs." In ⁧وِزَارَةُ الدَّاخِلِيَّةِ⁩ are the second term of theiḍāfa, to the genitive. 6. Chains Aiḍāfa can have three or more names. Only the last one can have the article or be a proper name; all previous items are without article; From the second on, they're all to the genitive. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧مَكْتَبُ مُدِيرِ الشُّرْطَةِ⁩ maktabu mudīri š-šurṭa the police director's office Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧رَئِيسُ بَلَدِيَّةِ مِيلَانُو⁩ raʾīsu baladiyyati Mīlānū the mayor of Milan (Lett. the head of the municipality of Milan) ⁧بَابُ بَيْتِ صَدِيقِي⁩ bābu bayti ṣadīqī the door of my friend's house It reads like a block. In a chain there is only one article, in the end: it is a useful signal to find where the nominal group ends up in a long title. 7. Iḍāfa with adjective The adjective cannot stand in the midst of aiḍāfa: goes after the whole building. It agrees with the name it refers to in general, determination and case: so you understand what name it speaks of. Arabic To whom the adjective refers Translation ⁧سَيَّارَةسَيَّارَةُ المُدِيرِ الجَدِيدَةُ⁩ (female, name) the new car of the director ⁧المُدِيرسَيَّارَةُ المُدِيرِ الجَدِيدِ⁩ (male, genitive) the car of the new director ⁧وَزِيروَزِيرُ الدَّاخِلِيَّةِ الإِيطَالِيُّ⁩ (male, name) the Italian Minister for the Interior ⁧مَبْنَىمَبْنَى الوِزَارَةِ القَدِيمُ⁩ (male, name) the old ministry building Without vowels sentences 1 and 2 are distinguished by gender ( ⁧الجديدة⁩ / ⁧الجديد⁩ ); When gender is the same, sometimes it only decides context. It is a real ambiguity of the unvocalized print: signal it when it counts. 8. Institutions and offices Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧وِزَارَةُ الدَّاخِلِيَّةِ⁩ wizāratu d-dāḫiliyya Ministry of the Interior ⁧وِزَارَةُ الخَارِجِيَّةِ⁩ wizāratu l-ḫāriǧiyya Ministry of Foreign Affairs ⁧وِزَارَةُ الدِّفَاعِ⁩ wizāratu d-difāʿ Ministry of Defence ⁧وِزَارَةُ العَدْلِ⁩ wizāratu l-ʿadl Ministry of Justice ⁧وِزَارَةُ الصِّحَّةِ⁩ wizāratu ṣ-ṣiḥḥa Ministry of Health ⁧وَزِيرُ الدَّاخِلِيَّةِ⁩ wazīru d-dāḫiliyya Minister for the Interior ⁧رَئِيسُ الوُزَرَاءِ⁩ raʾīsu l-wuzarāʾ Prime Minister Head of Ministers) ⁧رَئِيسُ الجُمْهُورِيَّةِ⁩ raʾīsu l-ǧumhūriyya President of the Republic ⁧مَجْلِسُ النُّوَّابِ⁩ maǧlisu n-nuwwāb Chamber of Deputies, Parliament ⁧مَجْلِسُ الأَمْنِ⁩ maǧlisu l-amn Security Council ⁧جَامِعَةُ الدُّوَلِ العَرَبِيَّةِ⁩ ǧāmiʿatu d-duwali l-ʿarabiyya League of Arab States ⁧الأُمَمُ المُتَّحِدَةُ⁩ al-umamu l-muttaḥida United Nations (name + adjective) ⁧سَفَارَةُ إِيطَالِيَا⁩ safāratu Īṭāliyā Embassy of Italy ⁧سَفِيرُ تُونِسَ⁩ safīru Tūnis Ambassador of Tunisia Two comments. In ⁧جَامِعَةُ الدُّوَلِ العَرَبِيَّةِ⁩ the adjective ⁧العَرَبِيَّة⁩ refers to ⁧الدُّوَل⁩ • the statuses (plural of what → female singular, A1-15) * The League of Arab States. Here ⁧جَامِعَة⁩ means "lega" , not "university." The names of the institutions of a country are translated by describing them: "The Italian Ministry of the Interior" is ⁧وِزَارَةُ الدَّاخِلِيَّةِ الإِيطَالِيَّةُ⁩ ; for bodies without a fixed Arab equivalent, the Arabic press uses different periphrases, and should be checked case by case. 9. Pronunciation -at and the ligament. Read the section table aloud 8 holding t of ⁧ة⁩ and linking termination to the article: wizāratu d-dāḫiliyya . Then read it again in the form of speech without desinence: wizārat ad-dāḫiliyya . ⁧الدِّفَاع⁩ , ⁧الصِّحَّة⁩ . Two šadda: that of the solar letter and that of the word ( ṣiḥḥa ). ⁧ج⁩ in ⁧جُمْهُورِيَّة⁩ , ⁧ء⁩ in ⁧الوُزَرَاء⁩ . ǧumhūriyya (ǧ as in the case of frosted, sucked; wuzarāʾ with the final glottidal occlusion, which you feel before a break. 10. title: Numbers from 0 a 10; Arabic and Indo-Arabic figures
text: Lesson overview Phone numbers, document numbers, plates, hotel rooms, age: the numbers appear in every practical exchange. The figures you know from L0-10; Now learn to tell them and write them in letters. In this unit you actively use numbers from 0 a 10 "by itself', i.e. by counting and dictating figures; the dozens and composite numbers you learn to say age and to recognize them. The agreement of the number with the numbered name, which in Arabic has its own rules, you will see it in A2: here you just need the rule of ⁧كَمْ⁩ ( A1-06). Item Details Code A1-11 Level A1 · Module A1.3 The Verb Prerequisites Module test A1.2 exceeded Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 29 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-11), voice synthesis script, your document with numbers (patent, card) to practice Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. say, read and write in letters the numbers from 0 a 10; 2. Moving from European figures to Indo-Arabs and vice versa; 3. to dictate and understand telephone, document and plate numbers, digit by digit; 4. Recognize numbers from 11 a 100 and the dozens; 5. tell your age and understand the age stated by others; 6. fill in the numerical fields of a form. Plan of the week. Day Activity 1 Dialogue 1 · section 1: numbers from 0 a 10 · vocabulary 2 Section 2: figures and direction · exercises 1–3 3 Section 3: phone, documents, plates · dialogue 2 · year 4 4 Section 4: 11 a 100 · section 5: age · exercises 5–6 5 Reading: a document and useful numbers · exercise 7 6 Dictation of numbers · listening · oral production 7 Unit verification · review Anki 1.
