Zero, two, one, two... and then? ⁧ثَلَاثَة، أَرْبَعَة، خَمْسَة، سِتَّة،⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ . ⁧سَبْعَة، ثَمَانِيَة⁩ Karīm: ṯalāṯa, arbaʿa, ḫamsa, sitta, sabʿa, ṯamāniya. Karīm: Three, four, five, six, seven, eight. ⁧ثَلَاثَة، تِسْعَة،⁩ : ⁧وَرَقْمِي⁩ . ⁧شُكْرًا⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: šukran. wa-raqmī: ṯalāṯa, tisʿa, ṣifrThank you. And my number: three, ... ⁧صِفْر⁩ Nine, zero... What to notice. The telephone numbers are digit-by-digit, with the numbers alone in the form used to count. The dialogue number is invented. ⁧ثُمَّ⁩ ṯumma It is then used to ask to continue. 2. Numbers from 0 a 10 European cipher Indo-Arab cipher Number Transliteration 0 ⁧٠⁩ ⁧صِفْر⁩ ṣifr 1 ⁧١⁩ ⁧وَاحِد⁩ wāḥid 2  ⁧اِثْنَان٢⁩ iṯnān 3  ⁧ثَلَاثَة٣⁩ ṯalāṯa 4  ⁧أَرْبَعَة٤⁩ arbaʿa 5  ⁧خَمْسَة٥⁩ ḫamsa 6  ⁧سِتَّة٦⁩ sitta 7  ⁧سَبْعَة٧⁩ sabʿa 8  ⁧ثَمَانِيَة٨⁩ ṯamāniya 9  ⁧تِسْعَة٩⁩ tisʿa 10 ⁧عَشَرَة١٠⁩ ʿašara Why they end up in ⁧ة⁩ . When you count (- one, two, three...) you use the shape with ⁧ة⁩ from 3 a 10. It is the basic form of the number. In front of a name the number changes ( ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ كُتُبٍ⁩ • three books • ⁧ثَلَاثُ سَيَّارَاتٍ⁩ • three cars: this is the rule of the agreement • on the contrary • that you will study in A2. For now, recognize her. ⁧وَاحِد⁩ and ⁧اِثْنَان⁩ have also the female: ⁧وَاحِدَة⁩ , ⁧اِثْنَتَان⁩ . They follow the name as adjectives: ⁧بِنْتٌ وَاحِدَةٌ⁩ One daughter is only one daughter.A1-09). ⁧صِفْر⁩ He gave English the word "cifra" and, through medieval Latin, "zero." The numbers. The direction is always from left to right, even in an Arabic line (L0-10). The ⁧٥⁩ ( 5) is a small circle; The zero ⁧٠⁩ It's a point. In handwriting 2 and 3 They look alike: ⁧٢⁩ has only one tooth at the top, ⁧٣⁩ Two. In texts without vowels the number is almost always written in digits; in letters only in legal texts, checks and formal documents. 3. Phone, documents, plates Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧مَا رَقْمُ هَاتِفِكِ؟⁩ mā raqmu hātifiki? What's your phone number? (to a woman) ⁧رَقْمُ جَوَازِ السَّفَرِ⁩ raqmu ǧawāzi s-safar passport number ⁧رَقْمُ بِطَاقَةِ الهُوِيَّةِ⁩ raqmu biṭāqati l-huwiyya ID card number ⁧لَوْحَةُ السَّيَّارَةِ⁩ lawḥatu s-sayyāra car plate ⁧رَقْمُ الغُرْفَةِ⁩ raqmu l-ġurfa room number ⁧رَقْمُ الطَّوَارِئِ⁩ raqmu ṭ-ṭawāriʾ emergency number How they dictate. Encrypt by digit, with the number alone paused: ṣifr, iṯnān, wāḥid… . Those who say often repeat the number twice; The writer reads it again: it is the safest practice in any language. The letters in the numbers. Passports and plates may contain letters. Egyptian plates, for example, have Arabic letters and Indo-Arabic digits: the part in letters reads from right to left, the part in digits from left to right. The letters are read by their name: ⁧ب⁩ bāʾ , ⁧س⁩ sīn . The Latin letters of passports are usually read by the English or French name of the letter, which varies from country to country: in case of doubt, they are written. In Egypt the national identity number is called ⁧الرَّقْمُ القَوْمِيُّ⁩ ar-raqmu l-qawmī ; in other countries ⁧رَقْمُ الهُوِيَّةِ⁩ . You'll recognize both formulas in the forms. 4. From 13 a 19: unit + ⁧عَشَرَ⁩ , all with vowel -a, no variations. The dozens are the units with -ūna (in genitive and accusative) -īna, A1-19): ⁧ثَلَاثُونَ⁩ , ⁧أَرْبَعُونَ⁩ ; 20 It's irregular. title: Dual and plural: pronouns and suffixes
text: Lesson overview So far you've spoken of "Io" , "Tu" , "Lui" , "Lei" . Arabic has eight other pronouns: in addition to the plural it has the dual, a form specifically for two "voi" and "their" two "s," and distinguishes the male from the female also to the plural. In this unit complete the table of independent pronouns and suffixes, learn to form the dual names and talk about groups: your team, your office, your class. Two weeks. Item Details Code A1-12 Level A1 · Module A1.3 The Verb Prerequisites A1-11 exceeded Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 30–31 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-12), voice synthesis script, tutor session in the second week Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. use all thirteen independent pronouns, including dual and female plural; 2. attack all suffixes to names and prepositions ( ⁧كِتَابُنَا، مَعَهُمْ، عِنْدَكُمْ⁩ ); 3. apply the -hum → -him step and -humā → -himā; 4. form the dual of names ( ⁧طَالِبَانِ⁩ / ⁧طَالِبَيْنِ⁩ ); 5. build nominal phrases with plural subject using the plurals you know as vocabulary; 6. present your team or office in 60 words. Two-week plan. Dialogue 1 · New students At the beginning of the lesson Salmā welcomes two new members. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧مَنْ أَنْتُمَا؟⁩ . ⁧مَسَاءُ الخَيْرِ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: masāʾu l-ḫayr. man antumā? Salmā: Good evening. Who are you two? . ⁧أَنَا يُوسُف، وَهُوَ سَمِير⁩ : ⁧يُوسُف⁩ . ⁧نَحْنُ طَالِبَانِ جَدِيدَانِ⁩ Yūsuf: anā Yūsuf, wa-huwa Samīr. naḥnu ṭālibāni ǧadīdān. Yūsuf: I am Yūsuf and he is Samīr. We're two new students. ⁧مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتُمَا؟⁩ ! ⁧أَهْلًا بِكُمَا⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: ahlan bikumā! min ayna antumā? SalmāWelcome! Samīr: I am Moroccan and Yūsuf is Tunisian. : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ (to Mary and Hudā) ⁧وَأَنْتُمَا؟⁩ ⁧هَلْ أَنْتُمَا زَمِيلَتَانِ؟⁩ Salmā: wa-antumā? hal antumā zamīlatān? Salmā: What about you two? Are you colleagues? . ⁧لَا، نَحْنُ صَدِيقَتَانِ⁩ : ⁧مَارْيَا⁩ Māryā: lā, naḥnu ṣadīqatān. No, we're friends. : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ (all) ⁧أَنْتُمُ الآنَ عَشَرَةُ⁩ ⁧طُلَّابٍ فِي الصَّفِّ⁩ ! Salmā: antumu l-āna ʿašaratu ṭullābin fī ṣ-ṣaff! Salmā: Now you are ten students in the class! ⁧وَأَيْنَ كُتُبُنَا الجَدِيدَةُ؟⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ Lūkā: wa-ayna kutubunā l-ǧadīda? Luca: And where are our new books? . ⁧كُتُبُكُمْ هُنَاكَ، عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: kutubukum hunāka, ʿalā ṭ-ṭāwila. Salmā: Your books are there, on the table. What to notice. Salmā use ⁧أَنْتُمَا⁩ You two with the couples and ⁧أَنْتُمْ⁩ You are with the whole class. The dual can also be seen in the names: ⁧طَالِبَانِ⁩ • two students: ⁧صَدِيقَتَانِ⁩ Two friends. ⁧كُتُبُنَا⁩ • our books • • ⁧كُتُبُكُمْ⁩ Your books are: the plural suffixes. In ⁧أَنْتُمُ الآنَ⁩ the m takes a support u in front of the alif waṣla, as in ⁧عَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ⁩ . 2. Independent pronouns: the full table  Singular Dual Plural 1per person ⁧أَنَا⁩ anā me — ⁧نَحْنُ⁩ naḥnu us 2a male ⁧أَنْتَ⁩ Do it. ⁧أَنْتُمَا⁩ antumā You two. ⁧أَنْتُمْ⁩ antum vole 2a female ⁧أَنْتِ⁩ Anti-tummy ⁧أَنْتُمَا⁩ antumā You two. ⁧أَنْتُنَّ⁩ (women) 3a male ⁧هُوَ⁩ Huwa him ⁧هُمَا⁩ humā The two of them ⁧هُمْ⁩ hum 3a female ⁧هِيَ⁩ Hiya her ⁧هُمَا⁩ humā The two of them ⁧هُنَّ⁩ Hunna their (women) The way they're used. • Mixed groups: male plural ( ⁧أَنْتُمْ⁩ , ⁧هُمْ⁩ ). One man in the group is enough. • Women only: ⁧أَنْتُنَّ⁩ , ⁧هُنَّ⁩ . Many people in the talk use masculine also for female groups; in the texts written on Female is regular. • Two people: the dual ⁧أَنْتُمَا⁩ , ⁧هُمَا⁩ , same for male and female. In the speech it often replaces with the plural; in the texts and in the news the dual is systematic. • ⁧نَحْنُ⁩ It applies to men and women, to two or more people. Plural of respect. In some official letters and formal speeches (Golfo, protocol) ⁧أَنْتُمْ⁩ It is used for one rank person only, and the sovereigns speak of themselves with ⁧نَحْنُ⁩ . Recognize it. It's not a mistake. 3. The dual of names It forms by adding -āni (name case) or -ayni (parent and accusative) to the singular. The ⁧ة⁩ becomes ⁧ت⁩ . Singular Dual name Genitive/accusative dual Translation  ⁧طَالِبَانِطَالِب⁩ ṭālibān ⁧طَالِبَيْنِ⁩ ṭālibayn two students  ⁧سَيَّارَتَانِسَيَّارَة⁩ sayyāratān ⁧سَيَّارَتَيْنِ⁩ sayyāratayn two cars  ⁧كِتَابَانِكِتَاب⁩ kitābān ⁧كِتَابَيْنِ⁩ kitābayn two books  ⁧زَمِيلَتَانِزَمِيلَة⁩ zamīlatān ⁧زَمِيلَتَيْنِ⁩ zamīlatayn two colleagues The dual is enough for itself. ⁧طَالِبَانِ⁩ It already means two students: ⁧اثْنَانِ⁩ is added only to insist. The adjective agrees with the dual: ⁧طَالِبَانِ جَدِيدَانِ⁩ , ⁧فِي سَيَّارَتَيْنِ صَغِيرَتَيْنِ⁩ . After preposition the dual goes to the genitive: ⁧مَعَ طَالِبَيْنِ⁩ With two students. In pause the final -i falls: ṭālibān , ṭālibayn . To be recognized. In front of a suffix or a second termiḍāfa the ⁧ن⁩ falls: ⁧كِتَابَا الطَّالِبِ⁩ The two books of the student are: ⁧يَدَاهُ⁩ His two hands are in. I will look into it in A2. 4. Plural subjects With a plural subject (people) the predicate goes to the plural. The plural names you already know as a vocabulary; the rules for training them are in A1-15. Arabic Transliteration Translation . ⁧نَحْنُ طُلَّابٌ⁩ naḥnu ṭullāb. We're students. . ⁧هُمْ زُمَلَاءُ⁩ hum zumalāʾ. They're colleagues. . ⁧أَنْتُمْ أَصْدِقَائِي⁩ antum aṣdiqāʾī. You're my friends. . ⁧هُمْ مُهَنْدِسُونَ مِصْرِيُّونَ⁩ hum muhandisūna miṣriyyūn. They're Egyptian engineers. . ⁧هُنَّ مُهَنْدِسَاتٌ⁩ hunna muhandisāt. I am an engineer (women). . ⁧نَحْنُ مَشْغُولُونَ اليَوْمَ⁩ naḥnu mašġūlūna l-yawm. We're busy today. Two models. Many adjectives and professional names and the nisba make plural with -ūna (male) and -āt (female): ⁧مُهَنْدِسُونَ⁩ , ⁧مِصْرِيُّونَ⁩ , ⁧مَشْغُولُونَ⁩ , ⁧مُهَنْدِسَاتٌ⁩ . Others have an inside plural to learn: ⁧طُلَّاب⁩ , ⁧زُمَلَاء⁩ , ⁧أَصْدِقَاء⁩ , ⁧رِجَال⁩ . It is the subject of A1-15. 5. The suffixes: the complete table  Singular Dual Plural 1per person ⁧كِتَابِي⁩ -ī — ⁧كِتَابُنَا⁩ -nā our book 2a male ⁧كِتَابُكَ⁩ -ka ⁧كِتَابُكُمَا⁩ -kumā ⁧كِتَابُكُمْ⁩ -kum your book 2a female ⁧كِتَابُكِ⁩ -ki ⁧كِتَابُكُمَا⁩ -kumā ⁧كِتَابُكُنَّ⁩ -Kunna 3a male ⁧كِتَابُهُ⁩ -hu ⁧كِتَابُهُمَا⁩ -humā ⁧كِتَابُهُمْ⁩ -hum their book 3a female ⁧كِتَابُهَا⁩ -hā ⁧كِتَابُهُمَا⁩ -humā ⁧كِتَابُهُنَّ⁩ -hunna Rules of A1-09 shall remain valid: ⁧ة⁩ → ⁧ت⁩ ( ⁧سَيَّارَتُنَا⁩ , ⁧مَدِينَتُهُمْ⁩ ); the vowel of the case before the suffix; name with suffix = determined. -hum → -him, -humā → -himā, -hunna → -hinna after i, ī, ay: ⁧فِي بَيْتِهِمْ⁩ fī beytihim at their home . ⁧عَلَيْهِمْ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ أَصْدِقَائِهِمْ⁩ . It's the same harmony as -hu → -hi. In front of the article -kum e -hum take a support u: ⁧كِتَابُكُمُ الجَدِيدُ⁩ kitābukumu l-ǧadīd , ⁧عَلَيْهِمُ⁩ ⁧السَّلَامُ⁩ . The hamza in front of the suffixes. In the -āʾ the hamza changes support according to the appropriate vowel (L0-09): ⁧زُمَلَاؤُنَا⁩ (name) ⁧مَعَ زُمَلَائِنَا⁩ (genitive). Reading doesn't change anything: it's always ʾ . 6. Prepositions with plural suffixes  us you (m.) vol (f.) You two. They (m.) They (f.) The two of them ⁧عِنْدَ⁩  ⁧عِنْدَكُنَّعِنْدَكُمْعِنْدَنَا⁩   ⁧عِنْدَهُنَّعِنْدَهُمْعِنْدَكُمَا⁩  ⁧عِنْدَهُمَا⁩ ⁧لِـ⁩  ⁧لَكُنَّلَكُمْلَنَا⁩   ⁧لَهُنَّلَهُمْلَكُمَا⁩  ⁧لَهُمَا⁩ ⁧مَعَ⁩  ⁧مَعَكُنَّمَعَكُمْمَعَنَا⁩   ⁧مَعَهُنَّمَعَهُمْمَعَكُمَا⁩  ⁧مَعَهُمَا⁩ ⁧فِي⁩  ⁧فِيكُنَّفِيكُمْفِينَا⁩   ⁧فِيهِنَّفِيهِمْفِيكُمَا⁩  ⁧فِيهِمَا⁩ ⁧عَلَى⁩  ⁧عَلَيْكُنَّعَلَيْكُمْعَلَيْنَا⁩   ⁧عَلَيْهِنَّعَلَيْهِمْعَلَيْكُمَا⁩  ⁧عَلَيْهِمَا⁩ ⁧مِنْ⁩  ⁧مِنْكُنَّمِنْكُمْمِنَّا⁩   ⁧مِنْهُنَّمِنْهُمْمِنْكُمَا⁩  ⁧مِنْهُمَا⁩ Now you understand in full ⁧السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ⁩ Peace on you and ⁧أَهْلًا بِكُمْ⁩ Welcome. 7. Pronunciation ⁧ح⁩ in ⁧نَحْنُ⁩ . naḥnu : ḥāʾ Faringale, not h. nahnu is a frequent mistake. The šadda of ⁧أَنْتُنَّ⁩ and ⁧هُنَّ⁩ . antunna , hunna: the double n is the only sign that distinguishes them when listening from ⁧أَنْتُمْ⁩ / ⁧هُمْ⁩ (in addition to m). The dual on pause. ṭālibān , ṣadīqatān : ā is long and the end n feels. In front of an adjective: ṭālibāni ǧadīdān . -kumā and -humā. Accento on the penultimate: kitābuKUmā , baytiHImā . 8. Examples in context Example Transliteration Translation Note ⁧هَلْ أَنْتُمْ مِنْ تُونِسَ؟⁩ hal antum min Tūnis? Are you from Tunisia? Mixed group . ⁧نَحْنُ وَفْدٌ مِنَ الوِزَارَةِ⁩ naḥnu wafdun mina l-wizāra. We're a delegation from the Ministry.  . ⁧هُمَا مُتَرْجِمَانِ مَغْرِبِيَّانِ⁩ humā mutarǧimāni maġribiyyān. They're two Moroccan interpreters. Dual + adjective . ⁧مَكْتَبُنَا فِي الطَّابِقِ الثَّانِي⁩ maktabunā fī ṭ-ṭābiqi ṯ-ṯānī. Our office is on the second floor.  ⁧لَا، هُوَ⁩ — ⁧هَلِ المُدِيرُ مَوْجُودٌ؟⁩ . ⁧مَعَ الضُّيُوفِ⁩ hali l-mudīru mawǧūd? — lā, huwa maʿa ḍ-ḍuyūf. Is the manager here? No, he's with the guests.  . ⁧عِنْدَهُمُ اجْتِمَاعٌ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ⁩ ʿindahumu ǧtimāʿun kulla yawm. They have a meeting every day. Support . ⁧أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا بِكُمْ فِي مِيلَانُو⁩ ahlan wa-sahlan bikum fī Mīlānū. Welcome to Milan.  . ⁧هٰذِهِ سَيَّارَتُهُمَا⁩ hāḏihi sayyāratuhumā. This is their car.  11. Reading · Our team Luca presents his working group. ⁧فِي⁩ . ⁧مَكْتَبُنَا فِي الطَّابِقِ الثَّانِي، وَهُوَ مَكْتَبٌ وَاسِعٌ⁩ . ⁧نَحْنُ فَرِيقٌ صَغِيرٌ فِي مَرْكَزِ الشُّرْطَةِ⁩ ⁧مُدِيرُنَا اسْمُهُ السَّيِّدُ⁩ . ⁧أَنَا وَهُدَى شُرْطِيَّانِ، وَكَرِيم وَسَارَة مُتَرْجِمَانِ⁩ : ⁧الفَرِيقِ أَرْبَعَةُ زُمَلَاءَ⁩ ⁧زُمَلَاؤُنَا فِي الطَّابِقِ الأَوَّلِ مَشْغُولُونَ دَائِمًا، وَعِنْدَهُمْ مَكْتَبٌ كَبِيرٌ⁩ . ⁧بِيَانْكِي، وَهُوَ رَجُلٌ هَادِئٌ⁩ ⁧هَلْ أَنْتُمْ أَيْضًا فَرِيقٌ صَغِيرٌ؟⁩ . ⁧عِنْدَنَا اجْتِمَاعٌ مَعَهُمْ كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ⁩ . ⁧وَحَوَاسِيبُ جَدِيدَةٌ⁩ Glossary: ⁧حَوَاسِيبُ جَدِيدَةٌ⁩ New computers (plural of what + female singular adjective: A1-15). 13. Listening Script A · Dialog 1 ⁧مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتُمَا؟ أَنَا⁩ ! ⁧أَهْلًا بِكُمَا⁩ . ⁧نَحْنُ طَالِبَانِ جَدِيدَانِ⁩ . ⁧مَنْ أَنْتُمَا؟ أَنَا يُوسُف، وَهُوَ سَمِير⁩ . ⁧مَسَاءُ الخَيْرِ⁩ . ⁧وَأَنْتُمَا؟ هَلْ أَنْتُمَا زَمِيلَتَانِ؟ لَا، نَحْنُ صَدِيقَتَانِ⁩ . ⁧مِنَ المَغْرِبِ، وَيُوسُف مِنْ تُونِسَ⁩ Script B · Who talks to whom? . ⁧أَهْلًا بِكُمْ فِي مِيلَانُو⁩ . ⁧١⁩ ⁧هَلْ أَنْتُمَا مِنْ مِصْرَ؟⁩ . ⁧٢⁩ . ⁧نَحْنُ مُتَرْجِمَاتٌ⁩ . ⁧٣⁩ . ⁧هُمْ زُمَلَاؤُنَا⁩ . ⁧٤⁩ ⁧أَيْنَ بَيْتُكُنَّ؟⁩ . ⁧٥⁩ . ⁧هُمَا طَبِيبَانِ⁩ . ⁧٦⁩ . ⁧سَيَّارَتُهُمْ أَمَامَ البَيْتِ⁩ . ⁧٧⁩ ⁧هَلْ عِنْدَكُمَا وَقْتٌ؟⁩ . ⁧٨⁩ 14. Oral production 1. Table aloud. Recite the thirteen pronouns and then suffixes on ⁧بَيْت⁩ and ⁧سَيَّارَة⁩ , without reading, in less than one minute. 2. With the tutor (second week): the tutor shows you photos of groups (two men, three women, one family, one team); presents each group with the right pronoun and suffix ( ⁧هُمَا⁩ … ⁧، بَيْتُهُمَا⁩ …). 3. My team. Present the text for the Exercise 10 and answer three tutor questions with ⁧أَنْتُمْ⁩ . 15. title: The imperfect to the singular: the essential verbs
text: Lesson overview Finally the verb. ⁧أَعْمَلُ⁩ • work • ⁧أَسْكُنُ⁩ ... ⁧أَدْرُسُ⁩ Study: with imperfection ( ⁧المُضَارِع⁩ al-muḍāriʿ ) tell you what you usually do, what you're doing and what you're going to do shortly. In this unit learn the singular conjugation, the order of the verbal phrase and the object complement, and tell a day's work. It is the most important unit of the module: it lasts two weeks. Item Details Code A1-13 Level A1 · Module A1.3 The Verb Prerequisites A1-12 exceeded Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 32–33 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-13), voice synthesis script, tutor session in the second week Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. recognize the root and form of a verb and seek its form of quote; 2. combine the verbs of the section to the singular imperfection 3, with the right vowel theme; 3. build the verbal sentence (verb + subject + complement) and use the complement accusative the subject matter; 4. ask questions with ⁧مَاذَا⁩ , ⁧أَيْنَ⁩ , ⁧مَتَى⁩ + verb; 5. describe your day and understand another person's routine; 6. write 60 words about your routine. Two-week plan. title: The imperfect in the plural; the denial withلَا‎
text: Lesson overview We study, we work, they live in Rome, we don't speak Arabic. With this unity complete the imperfect, adding the plural and the dual, and learn to deny it by ⁧لَا⁩ . You will also see a rule that surprises the Italians: when the verb precedes a plural subject it remains to the singular ( ⁧يَدْرُسُ الطُّلَّابُ⁩ • students study •). Two weeks. Item Details Code A1-14 Level A1 · Module A1.3 The Verb Prerequisites A1-13 exceeded Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 34–35 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-14), voice synthesis script, tutor session in the second week Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. to unite the imperfect in all thirteen persons; 2. grant the verb with a plural subject before and after the verb; 3. deny the present with ⁧لَا⁩ and respond negatively; 4. use verbs ⁧يَتَكَلَّمُ⁩ , ⁧يَتَعَلَّمُ⁩ , ⁧يُرِيدُ⁩ , ⁧يَقُولُ⁩ , ⁧يَزُورُ⁩ and other frequent verbs; 5. understand a text about a family and a dialogue with negative phrases; 6. tell what you do and what you do not do and your family or your group. Two-week plan. Dialogue 1 · How do you study? Salmā asks the class how he studies at home. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧مَاذَا تَدْرُسُونَ فِي البَيْتِ؟⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: māḏā tadrusūna fī l-bayt? Salmā: What are you studying at home? ⁧نَقْرَأُ الدُّرُوسَ وَنَكْتُبُ⁩ : ⁧يُوسُف⁩ . ⁧التَّمَارِينَ⁩ Yūsuf: naqraʾu d-durūsa wa-naktubu t- tamārīn. Yūsuf: We read the lessons and write the exercises. ⁧هَلْ تَسْمَعُونَ الحِوَارَاتِ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧كُلَّ يَوْمٍ؟⁩ Salmā: hal tasmaʿūna l-ḥiwārāti kulla yawm? Salmā: Do you listen to dialogues every day? ⁧نَعَمْ، نَسْمَعُهَا فِي السَّيَّارَةِ⁩ : ⁧يُوسُف⁩ . ⁧أَوْ فِي البَيْتِ⁩ Yūsuf: naʿam, nasmaʿuhā fī s-sayyārati aw fī l-bayt. Yūsuf: Yes, we listen in the car or at home. ⁧وَأَنْتُمَا يَا مَارْيَا وَهُدَى؟⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: wa-antumā yā Māryā wa-Hudā? Salmā: And you two, Mary and Hudā? ⁧نَقْرَأُ⁩ . ⁧نَحْنُ نَدْرُسُ مَعًا⁩ : ⁧مَارْيَا⁩ . ⁧النُّصُوصَ وَنَتَكَلَّمُ بِالعَرَبِيَّةِ⁩ Māryā: naḥnu nadrusu maʿan. naqraʾu n- nuṣūṣa wa-natakallamu bi-l-ʿarabiyya. We study together. We read the lyrics and speak Arabic. ⁧وَلُوكَا وَكَرِيم؟⁩ ! ⁧مُمْتَازٌ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: mumtāz! wa-Lūkā wa-Karīm? SalmāGreat! And Luke and Karīm? ⁧هُمَا يَعْمَلَانِ فِي المَكْتَبِ⁩ : ⁧مَارْيَا⁩ . ⁧نَفْسِهِ، وَيَتَكَلَّمَانِ بِالعَرَبِيَّةِ أَحْيَانًا⁩ Māryā: humā yaʿmalāni fī l-maktabi nafsihi, wa-yatakallamāni bi-l-ʿarabiyyati aḥyānan. They work in the same office and sometimes speak Arabic. What to notice. Reading Reading 1 · The family of Salmā in Milan ⁧هِيَ مُدَرِّسَةٌ،⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى وَزَوْجُهَا عَادِل يَعْمَلَانِ فِي المَدِينَةِ⁩ . ⁧تَعِيشُ عَائِلَةُ سَلْمَى فِي مِيلَانُو⁩ . ⁧صَبَاحًا يَخْرُجَانِ مِنَ البَيْتِ مُبَكِّرًا، وَبِنْتُهُمَا نُور تَذْهَبُ إِلَى المَدْرَسَةِ مَعَ أَبِيهَا⁩ . ⁧وَهُوَ طَبِيبٌ⁩ ⁧نُور تَتَكَلَّمُ العَرَبِيَّةَ وَالإِيطَالِيَّةَ، وَتَتَعَلَّمُ⁩ . ⁧مَسَاءً يَأْكُلُونَ مَعًا، وَيَتَكَلَّمُونَ بِالعَرَبِيَّةِ فِي البَيْتِ⁩ ⁧فِي العُطْلَةِ يَزُورُونَ أَصْدِقَاءَهُمْ، وَأَحْيَانًا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ مَعَ العَائِلَةِ فِي⁩ . ⁧الإِنْجْلِيزِيَّةَ فِي المَدْرَسَةِ⁩ . ⁧القَاهِرَةِ بِالهَاتِفِ⁩ Reading 2 · Two roommates ⁧يُوسُف يَخْرُجُ مُبَكِّرًا، لٰكِنْ⁩ . ⁧يُوسُف وَسَمِير يَسْكُنَانِ فِي بَيْتٍ صَغِيرٍ قَرِيبٍ مِنَ الجَامِعَةِ⁩ ⁧سَمِير لَا يَطْبُخُ،⁩ . ⁧يَشْرَبُ الشَّايَ فَقَطْ⁩ : ⁧يُوسُف لَا يَشْرَبُ القَهْوَةَ⁩ . ⁧سَمِير لَا يَخْرُجُ قَبْلَ الظُّهْرِ⁩ ⁧هُمَا لَا يَتَكَلَّمَانِ كَثِيرًا صَبَاحًا، لٰكِنْ مَسَاءً يَأْكُلَانِ مَعًا وَيَتَكَلَّمَانِ عَنِ⁩ ! ⁧وَلَا يَعْرِفُ أَيْنَ المَطْبَخُ⁩ ⁧أَنْتُمَا مُخْتَلِفَانِ جِدًّا، لٰكِنْ أَنْتُمَا⁩ » : ⁧أَصْدِقَاؤُهُمَا يَقُولُونَ⁩ . ⁧الدِّرَاسَةِ وَعَنْ تُونِسَ وَالمَغْرِبِ⁩ .« ⁧صَدِيقَانِ جَيِّدَانِ⁩ Glossary: ⁧المَطْبَخ⁩ al-maṭbaḫ The kitchen (A1-16). 13. Listening Script A · Dialog 2 ⁧مَا المُشْكِلَةُ؟ أَبْحَثُ عَنْ فُنْدُقِي، لٰكِنْ لَا أَعْرِفُ⁩ . ⁧أَبِي تُونِسِيٌّ⁩ . ⁧عَفْوًا، هَلْ تَتَكَلَّمِينَ العَرَبِيَّةَ؟ نَعَمْ، قَلِيلًا⁩ . ⁧هُوَ قَرِيبٌ مِنْ مَحَطَّةٍ كَبِيرَةٍ⁩ . ⁧مَا اسْمُ الفُنْدُقِ؟ لَا أَذْكُرُ⁩ . ⁧العُنْوَانَ⁩ Script B · Who? . ⁧نَدْرُسُ العَرَبِيَّةَ مَسَاءً⁩ . ⁧١⁩ ⁧هَلْ تَعْمَلُونَ هُنَا؟⁩ . ⁧٢⁩ . ⁧يَسْكُنُونَ فِي رُومَا⁩ . ⁧٣⁩ . ⁧يَتَكَلَّمْنَ الفَرَنْسِيَّةَ⁩ . ⁧٤⁩ . ⁧هُمَا يَشْرَبَانِ الشَّايَ⁩ . ⁧٥⁩ . ⁧لَا نَعْرِفُ⁩ . ⁧٦⁩ . ⁧لَا يَفْهَمُ الطُّلَّابُ السُّؤَالَ⁩ . ⁧٧⁩ ⁧هَلْ تُرِيدَانِ قَهْوَةً؟⁩ . ⁧٨⁩ 14. Oral production 1. Table aloud. Recites the thirteen forms of ⁧يَدْرُسُ⁩ , then ⁧يَتَكَلَّمُ⁩ , less than 30 Seconds each. 2. Yes or no (with tutor): the tutor asks ten questions of the type ⁧هَلْ تَعْمَلُ يَوْمَ الأَحَدِ؟⁩ ; answer with full sentences, alternating yes and no. Then ask the tutor what his family does ( ⁧هَلْ يَعْمَلُونَ⁩ … ⁧؟ هَلْ يَتَكَلَّمُونَ⁩ … ⁧؟⁩ ). 3. At the bar. Act the exercise dialogue 6, with the tutor as a waiter. 15. Typical errors Error Correction ⁧يَدْرُسُونَ الطُّلَّابُ⁩ : ⁧يَدْرُسُ الطُّلَّابُ⁩ singular verb before subject ⁧الطُّلَّابُ يَدْرُسُ⁩ : ⁧الطُّلَّابُ يَدْرُسُونَ⁩ after the subject agrees in the number ⁧لَا أَعْرِفُلَيْسَ أَعْرِفُ⁩ : ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ denies nominal sentences (A1-16) Confound -ūna and -na ⁧يَدْرُسُونَ⁩ (male) · ⁧يَدْرُسْنَ⁩ (female) ⁧أُرِيدُ قَهْوَةٌ⁩ : ⁧أُرِيدُ قَهْوَةً⁩ supplement to the charge Error Correction yatakalamu yatakallamu : l double Use ⁧تَتَكَلَّمُ⁩ with a woman ⁧تَتَكَلَّمِينَ⁩ 16. Flashcard Deck A1, tag A1-14: 22 rumors. For each new verb, the paper shows the form "lui": di' aloud "io" , "tu" feminine and "loro" (the three forms of the section table) 4). 17. Unit verification Twenty points; Exceeding at least 16. Conjugation (6 (paragraphs) 1. We work. 2. you (m.) live · 3. They drink (m.) · 4. The two of them go · 5. you (f.) understand · 6. We speak B · Agreement (4 (paragraphs) 7. Employees work here (verb before). · 8. Employees work here (subject first). · 9. The two students study together. · 10. Guests want tea. C · Denial (6 (paragraphs) 11. I don't know. · 12. I don't understand the question. · 13. She doesn't speak Italian (she). · 14. We don't live in Rome. · 15. They don't drink coffee or tea. · 16. No, I don't work at night. D · Correction (4 (paragraphs) 17. ⁧يَعْمَلُونَ المُهَنْدِسُونَ⁩ · 18. ⁧هُمْ يَكْتُبُ⁩ · 19. ⁧لَيْسَ نَفْهَمُ⁩ · 20. ⁧أُرِيدُ مَاءٌ⁩ 18. To switch to A1-15 • ☐ Verification ≥ 16/20. • ☐ Recite the imperfect complete with two verbs without reading. • ☐ Apply singular verb rule + plural subject. • ☐ Use ⁧لَا أَعْرِفُ⁩ , ⁧لَا أَفْهَمُ⁩ , ⁧أُرِيدُ⁩ ... in sessions with the tutor. • ☐ Carte Anki A1-14 all seen at least once.

title: Family and professions; the healthy plural
text: Lesson overview ⁧مُهَنْدِسُونَ⁩ • Engineers • ⁧مُهَنْدِسَاتٌ⁩ • Engineer • ⁧طُلَّابٌ⁩ The Arabic form the plural in two ways. The healthy plural adds a desinence (-ūna, -āt) and leave the word intact; The plural over change the word from within. In this unity you learn the healthy plural, a first group of plural traits and the most important rule of agreement of Arabic grammar: the plurals of things agree to the singular feminine. The vocabulary is that of the professions and family. Item Details Code A1-15 Level A1 · Module A1.3 The Verb Prerequisites A1-14 exceeded Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 36 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-15), script for speech synthesis Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. form the healthy male plural (-ūna / -īna) and female (-ātun / -ātin); 2. to recognize the most frequent plurals and learn them with the singular; 3. to give adjectives, verbs and pronouns with plurals of people and things; 4. use ⁧هٰؤُلَاءِ⁩ for people and ⁧هٰذِهِ⁩ for things in the plural; 5. name about twenty professions and describe your work and that of your colleagues and family members. Plan of the week. Day Activity 1 Dialog · section 1: the healthy male plural · lexicon (first half) 2 Section 2: the healthy female plural · exercises 1–2 3 Section 3: pluralities over the years 3 4 Section 4: the agreement of the plurals · years 4–5 5 Reading · lexicon (second half) · exercises 6–7 6 Writing · listening · oral production 7 Unit verification · module review A1.3 1. Dialogue · An interview at work Laylā prepares an article on women in the Italian police and interview Hudā. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧مَا عَمَلُكِ فِي المَرْكَزِ يَا⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ ⁧هُدَى؟⁩ Laylā: mā ʿamaluki fī l-markazi yā Hudā? Laylā: What work do you do at the police station, Hudā? ⁧أَعْمَلُ فِي⁩ . ⁧أَنَا شُرْطِيَّةٌ⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧فَرِيقٍ صَغِيرٍ مَعَ ضَابِطَيْنِ⁩ . ⁧وَمُتَرْجِمَيْنِ⁩ Hudā: anā šurṭiyya. aʿmalu fī farīqin ṣaġīrin maʿa ḍābiṭayni wa-mutarǧimayn. HudāI'm a cop. I work in a small team with two officers and two interpreters. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧هَلْ فِي المَرْكَزِ شُرْطِيَّاتٌ⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ ⁧كَثِيرَاتٌ؟⁩ Laylā: hal fī l-markazi šurṭiyyātun kaṯīrāt? Laylā: Are there many policemen at the police station? . ⁧نَعَمْ، وَبَعْضُهُنَّ ضَابِطَاتٌ⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ Hudā: naʿam, wa-baʿḍuhunna ḍābiṭāt. Hudā: Yes, and some are official. ⁧وَالمُتَرْجِمُونَ؟ مِنْ أَيْنَ⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ ⁧هُمْ؟⁩ Laylā: wa-l-mutarǧimūn? min ayna hum? Laylā: What about the interpreters? Where did they come from? ⁧المُتَرْجِمُونَ مِنْ بِلَادٍ⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ ⁧مِنَ المَغْرِبِ وَمِصْرَ⁩ : ⁧مُخْتَلِفَةٍ⁩ . ⁧هُمْ مُهِمُّونَ جِدًّا لِعَمَلِنَا⁩ . ⁧وَسُورِيَا⁩ Hudā: al-mutarǧimūna min bilādin muḫtalifa: mina l-Maġribi wa-Miṣra wa- Sūriyā. hum muhimmūna ǧiddan li- ʿamalinā. Hudā: Interpreters come from different countries: Morocco, Egypt and Syria. They're very important to our work. ⁧وَهَلِ العَمَلُ صَعْبٌ؟⁩ : ⁧لَيْلَى⁩ Laylā: wa-hali l-ʿamalu ṣaʿb? Laylā: And the job is difficult? ⁧السَّاعَاتُ طَوِيلَةٌ،⁩ . ⁧أَحْيَانًا⁩ : ⁧هُدَى⁩ . ⁧لٰكِنِ الزُّمَلَاءُ مُمْتَازُونَ⁩ Hudā: aḥyānan. as-sāʿātu ṭawīlatun, lākini z-zumalāʾu mumtāzūn. Hudā: Sometimes. Times (Lett. The hours) are long, but colleagues are excellent. What to notice. For people the adjective is plural: ⁧شُرْطِيَّاتٌ كَثِيرَاتٌ⁩ , ⁧المُتَرْجِمُونَ مُهِمُّونَ⁩ , ⁧الزُّمَلَاءُ مُمْتَازُونَ⁩ . For things it's female singular: ⁧بِلَادٍ مُخْتَلِفَةٍ⁩ • different countries • ⁧السَّاعَاتُ طَوِيلَةٌ⁩ The hours are long. ⁧ضَابِطَيْنِ⁩ and ⁧مُتَرْجِمَيْنِ⁩ They're dual to the genitive after ⁧مَعَ⁩ ( A1-12). 2. The healthy male plural It is used for men (or mixed groups) indicated by participles, adjectives and nisba: ⁧مُدَرِّس⁩ , ⁧مُهَنْدِس⁩ , ⁧مُوَظَّف⁩ , ⁧مِصْرِيّ⁩ , ⁧مَشْغُول⁩ . Case Desinence Example Transliteration Name (subject, predicate) ⁧ـُونَ⁩ -ūna . ⁧المُدَرِّسُونَ هُنَا⁩ al-mudarrisūna hunā Genitive and accusative (after preposition, object) ⁧ـِينَ⁩ -īna ⁧أَعْرِفُ⁩ · ⁧مَعَ المُدَرِّسِينَ⁩ ⁧المُدَرِّسِينَ⁩ maʿa l-mudarrisīn · aʿrifu l- mudarrisīn Two cases, not three. The healthy male and dual plural have a form for the name and one for all other cases: -ūna/-īna, -āni/-ayni. Pause: -ūn , -īn . Without ⁧ن⁩ iniḍāfa and with the suffixes (recognize): ⁧مُوَظَّفُو الوِزَارَةِ⁩ • the employees of the Ministry • ⁧مُدَرِّسُوكَ⁩ Your teachers will be ⁧مَعَ مُوَظَّفِي البَنْكِ⁩ With bank employees. The final alif of ⁧مُوَظَّفُو⁩ It's not pronounced. It doesn't apply to all male names. ⁧طَالِب⁩ , ⁧طَبِيب⁩ , ⁧زَمِيل⁩ , ⁧رَجُل⁩ they have multiple fractures (section 4). Male healthy plural is typical of the words that begin with ⁧مُـ⁩ (participants) and nisba. 3. The healthy female plural It forms by removing the ⁧ة⁩ and adding -āt . Case Desinence Example Transliteration Name / ⁧ـَاتٌ⁩ ⁧مُدَرِّسَاتٌـَاتُ⁩ ⁧المُدَرِّسَاتُ⁩ · mudarrisātun · al-mudarrisātu Genitive and accusative / ⁧ـَاتٍ⁩ ⁧مَعَ مُدَرِّسَاتٍـَاتِ⁩ ⁧أَعْرِفُ المُدَرِّسَاتِ⁩ · maʿa mudarrisātin · aʿrifu l-mudarrisāti The accusative in -i. It is the only exception to the system of cases that you have seen so far: in the female plural the accusative has not -a but -i, like the genitive. ⁧أَعْرِفُ المُدَرِّسَاتِ⁩ , not ⁧المدرساتَ⁩ ». Not just women. -āt form the plural of many words in ⁧ة⁩ ( ⁧سَيَّارَات⁩ , ⁧جَامِعَات⁩ , ⁧وِزَارَات⁩ , ⁧مُشْكِلَات⁩ ), of some male ( ⁧اِجْتِمَاعَات⁩ , ⁧مَطَارَات⁩ , ⁧حِوَارَات⁩ ) and almost all foreign words ( ⁧تِلِفِزْيُونَات⁩ • Televisions). It is the plural reserve of modern language. 4. Pluralities Many names form the plural changing vowels and internal structure, starting from the same root. The schemes are numerous; The most frequent ones are recognized soon. Singular Plural Pattern Meaning  ⁧طُلَّابطَالِب⁩ fuʿʿāl student ⁧عَامِل⁩ ⁧عُمَّال⁩ fuʿʿāl worker, worker ⁧تَاجِر⁩ ⁧تُجَّار⁩ fuʿʿāl trader ⁧ضَابِط⁩ ⁧ضُبَّاط⁩ fuʿʿāl official ⁧زَمِيل⁩ ⁧زُمَلَاء⁩ fuʿalāʾ colleague ⁧خَبِير⁩ ⁧خُبَرَاء⁩ fuʿalāʾ expert ⁧وَزِير⁩ ⁧وُزَرَاء⁩ fuʿalāʾ Minister ⁧طَبِيب⁩ ⁧أَطِبَّاء⁩ afʿilāʾ doctor ⁧صَدِيق⁩ ⁧أَصْدِقَاء⁩ afʿilāʾ friend  ⁧بُيُوتبَيْت⁩ fuʿūl home ⁧دَرْس⁩ ⁧دُرُوس⁩ fuʿūl lesson  ⁧كُتُبكِتَاب⁩ fuʿul book  ⁧مُدُنمَدِينَة⁩ fuʿul city ⁧رَجُل⁩ ⁧رِجَال⁩ fiʿāl man ⁧وَلَد⁩ ⁧أَوْلَاد⁩ afʿāl boy, son  ⁧مَكَاتِبمَكْتَب⁩ mafāʿil office ⁧مَدْرَسَة⁩ ⁧مَدَارِس⁩ mafāʿil school How to learn them. The plural over is learned together with the singular: in the vocabulary of this volume it is always indicated, and in Anki the paper reports it. With time you will recognize the patterns and you can guess many plurals; the complete analysis of the schemes is in A2 and B1. Diptotes. Some schemes (fuʿalāʾ, afʿilāʾ, mafāʿil) do not take tanwīn and to the indeterminate genitive have -a: ⁧مِنْ زُمَلَاءَ⁩ , ⁧فِي مَكَاتِبَ⁩ ( A1-08). 5. The agreement of the parties The plural indicates Adjective Word Proname Demonstratory persons plural plural (if after the subject) / ⁧هُمْ⁩ ⁧هٰؤُلَاءِهُنَّ⁩ things, animals, concepts female singular female singular  ⁧هٰذِهِهِيَ⁩ Example Translation . ⁧المُهَنْدِسُونَ مِصْرِيُّونَ⁩ Engineers are Egyptians. . ⁧الطُّلَّابُ جَدِيدُونَ⁩ / ⁧الطُّلَّابُ جُدُدٌ⁩ The students are new. (two possible plurals) . ⁧السَّيَّارَاتُ جَدِيدَةٌ⁩ The cars are new. . ⁧الكُتُبُ عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ، وَهِيَ صَعْبَةٌ⁩ The books are on the table, and they're hard. . ⁧هٰؤُلَاءِ زُمَلَائِي⁩ These are my colleagues. . ⁧هٰذِهِ كُتُبِي⁩ These are my books. . ⁧الدُّرُوسُ تَبْدَأُ صَبَاحًا⁩ / ⁧الطُّلَّابُ يَدْرُسُونَ⁩ Students study / classes start in the morning. Because. For Arabic grammar a set of things is perceived as a unique mass, treated as a singular feminine. Remember this every time you read a plural: ...person or what? The rule also applies to healthy plurals of things: ⁧الوِزَارَاتُ مُهِمَّةٌ⁩ The ministries are important. Adjectives for people in the plural can be healthy or between: ⁧كَبِير⁩ → ⁧كِبَار⁩ , ⁧جَدِيد⁩ → ⁧جُدُد⁩ . If you do not know the plural over, the healthy plural ( ⁧جَدِيدُونَ⁩ ) is generally understandable, but in the vocabulary you find the most used form. 6. The professions Singular Plural Meaning ⁧ضَابِط⁩ ⁧ضُبَّاط⁩ Officer (police, army) ( ⁧المُحَامِي⁩ ) ⁧مُحَامٍ⁩ ⁧مُحَامُونَ⁩ lawyer ( ⁧القَاضِي⁩ ) ⁧قَاضٍ⁩ ⁧قُضَاة⁩ Judge  ⁧مُحَاسِبُونَمُحَاسِب⁩ accountant, accountant ⁧عَامِل⁩ ⁧عُمَّال⁩ worker, worker  ⁧سَائِقُونَسَائِق⁩ driver ⁧تَاجِر⁩ ⁧تُجَّار⁩ trader  ⁧مُبَرْمِجُونَمُبَرْمِج⁩ programmer ⁧خَبِير⁩ ⁧خُبَرَاء⁩ expert  ⁧بَاحِثُونَبَاحِث⁩ researcher  ⁧مُرَاسِلُونَمُرَاسِل⁩ corresponding (journalism)  ⁧مُحَلِّلُونَمُحَلِّل⁩ analyst  ⁧طَيَّارُونَطَيَّار⁩ pilot  ⁧مُتَقَاعِدُونَمُتَقَاعِد⁩ Pensioned ⁧مُحَامٍ⁩ and ⁧قَاضٍ⁩ . No article ends in tanwīn -in; with the article have -ī: ⁧المُحَامِي⁩ , ⁧القَاضِي⁩ . It is the 'defective' model of ⁧مَقْهًى⁩ and ⁧مَبْنًى⁩ , with the i in place of a. The female is regular: ⁧مُحَامِيَة⁩ , ⁧قَاضِيَة⁩ . Working as... in Arabic is said to be ⁧أَعْمَلُ مُحَاسِبًا⁩ "work as an accountant" or simply ⁧أَنَا مُحَاسِبٌ⁩ . 7. Pronunciation -ūna / -īna. The difference is in the long vowel: mudarrisūna / mudarrisīna . Pause -ūn / -īn : Here ū and ī Well, that's very distinct. -ātun / -ātin. muhandisātun , maʿa muhandisātin : ā It's long and it has an accent. The doubles of the plurals over. ⁧طُلَّاب⁩ ṭullāb , ⁧ضُبَّاط⁩ ḍubbāṭ , ⁧تُجَّار⁩ tuǧǧār , ⁧عُمَّال⁩ ʿummāl : the double central consonant is the sign of the scheme fuʿʿāl. ⁧ض⁩ and ⁧ط⁩ in ⁧ضَابِط⁩ . Two emphasis in the same word: ḍābiṭ , plural ḍubbāṭ . 8. title: House and city; the denial withلَيْسَ‎
text: Lesson overview The house is not large ,   , I am not Egyptian , , there is the elevator , to deny a nominal phrase the Arabic uses ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ , a word that combines like a verb and that puts the predicate to the accusative: . ⁧البَيْتُ لَيْسَ كَبِيرًا⁩ In this unit you learn it along with the vocabulary of the house and neighborhood, read real estate ads and describe the place where you live. Two weeks. Item Details Code A1-16 Level A1 · Module A1.4 Daily life Prerequisites Module test A1.3 exceeded Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 38–39 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-16), vocal synthesis script, a plant of your home, session with the tutor in the second week Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. deny a nominal sentence with ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ and place the predicate on the accusative; 2. conjugate ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ with all singular and plural pronouns; 3. choose between ⁧لَا⁩ (verb) and ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ (rated sentence); 4. use ⁧غَيْر⁩ to deny an adjective ( ⁧غَيْرُ مَفْرُوشَةٍ⁩ ); 5. read a rental announcement and ask an agency for information; 6. describe your home and neighborhood in 70 words. Two-week plan. Day Activity 1 Reading 1: the announcement · vocabulary of the house 2 Section 1: ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ and the predicate to the accusative · exercises 1–2 3 Dialogue 1 to the agency · section 2: There is no exercise 3 4 Section 3: the conjugation of ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ (singular) · year 4 5 Pronunciation · describe your home by voice 6 Listening: script A · exercise 10 (part a) 7 Review Anki 8 Section 3: the conjugation of ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ (plural and dual) · exercise 5 9 Section 4: ⁧لَا⁩ or ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ ? · section 5: ⁧غَيْر⁩ · financial years 6–7 10 Neighborhood lexicon · reading 2 · year 8 11 Writing - My Neighborhood 12 Session with tutor · listening to directions (script B) 13 Unit verification 14 Recovery · Anki Reading 1 · An announcement ⁧الشَّقَّةُ فِي الطَّابِقِ الثَّالِثِ، وَفِي⁩ . ⁧شَقَّةٌ فِي حَيٍّ هَادِئٍ قَرِيبٍ مِنْ وَسَطِ المَدِينَةِ⁩ : ⁧لِلْإِيجَارِ⁩ ⁧فِيهَا غُرْفَتَا نَوْمٍ، وَغُرْفَةُ جُلُوسٍ وَاسِعَةٌ، وَمَطْبَخٌ حَدِيثٌ، وَحَمَّامٌ، وَشُرْفَةٌ⁩ . ⁧العِمَارَةِ مِصْعَدٌ⁩ . ⁧مَوْقِفُ الحَافِلَةِ أَمَامَ العِمَارَةِ⁩ . ⁧٩٠٠ يُورُو شَهْرِيًّا⁩ : ⁧الإِيجَارُ⁩ . ⁧الشَّقَّةُ غَيْرُ مَفْرُوشَةٍ⁩ . ⁧صَغِيرَةٌ⁩ Glossary: ⁧لِلْإِيجَارِ⁩ "Rental" (Lett. for rent) · ⁧العِمَارَة⁩ The palace, the condominium ⁧غُرْفَتَا نَوْمٍ⁩ Two bedrooms (dual in theiḍāfa: ⁧ن⁩ falls, A1-12) · ⁧غَيْرُ مَفْرُوشَةٍ⁩ Unfurnished (section 5) · ⁧٩٠٠⁩ = ⁧تِسْعُمِئَةِ⁩ tisʿumiʾati · ⁧شَهْرِيًّا⁩ • per month • per month • per month • per month • per month 1. : ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ deny the nominal sentence Sentence Negative phrase Translation . ⁧البَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ⁩ . ⁧البَيْتُ لَيْسَ كَبِيرًا⁩ The house is not big.  . ⁧لَيْسَ البَيْتُ كَبِيرًا⁩ (same meaning) . ⁧الشَّقَّةُ مَفْرُوشَةٌ⁩ . ⁧الشَّقَّةُ لَيْسَتْ مَفْرُوشَةً⁩ The apartment is not furnished. . ⁧أَنَا مِصْرِيٌّ⁩ . ⁧لَسْتُ مِصْرِيًّا⁩ I'm not Egyptian. . ⁧هُوَ فِي البَيْتِ⁩ . ⁧لَيْسَ فِي البَيْتِ⁩ He's not home. . ⁧المَحَطَّةُ قَرِيبَةٌ⁩ . ⁧المَحَطَّةُ لَيْسَتْ قَرِيبَةً⁩ The station is not near. Three rules. 1. The predicate goes to the accusative: ⁧كَبِيرٌ⁩ → ⁧كَبِيرًا⁩ , ⁧مَفْرُوشَةٌ⁩ → ⁧مَفْرُوشَةً⁩ . It is the only change in form of sentence. 2. If the predicate is a complement with preposition or adverb ( ⁧فِي البَيْتِ⁩ , ⁧هُنَا⁩ ) nothing changes: the Preposition already holds his case. 3. ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ agrees with the subject: ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ for a male subject, ⁧لَيْسَتْ⁩ for a female, ⁧لَسْتُ⁩ for . The subject pronoun generally fails, because ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ it contains: ⁧لَسْتُ مِصْرِيًّا⁩ I'm not Egyptian. Because the accused. ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ is originally a verb (to not be) of the same family as ⁧كَانَ⁩ • to be: (A2): These verbs leave the subject to the name and put the predicate to the accusative. You'll find it in A1-19. In texts without vowels the predicate to the accusative can only be seen when there is the aliif of tanwīn: . ⁧البيت ليس كبيرا⁩ It's a good clue to recognize a nominal negation. 2. There's no squirrel and I don't have any In the sentences ... there is / there are (A1-04) the subject comes after the complement and remains at the name: Arabic Transliteration Translation . ⁧لَيْسَ فِي العِمَارَةِ مِصْعَدٌ⁩ laysa fī l-ʿimārati miṣʿad. There's no elevator in the building. . ⁧لَيْسَ هُنَاكَ مَوْقِفٌ قَرِيبٌ⁩ laysa hunāka mawqifun qarīb. There's no stop nearby. . ⁧لَيْسَ عِنْدِي سَيَّارَةٌ⁩ laysa ʿindī sayyāra. I don't have a car. Here ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ it always remains to the singular male, whatever the subject: it is a fixed form, as in A1-08. 3. The conjugation of ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ it combines with the desinences of the perfect (which you will study in A1-18). When desinence begins by consonant, the root shortens in ⁧لَسْ⁩ -. Person Form Example me ⁧لَسْتُ⁩ lastu . ⁧لَسْتُ مَشْغُولًا⁩ I'm not busy. you (m.) ⁧لَسْتَ⁩ last . ⁧لَسْتَ وَحْدَكَ⁩ You're not alone. you (f.) ⁧لَسْتِ⁩ last . ⁧لَسْتِ مُتْعَبَةً⁩ You're not tired. him ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ laysa . ⁧لَيْسَ هُنَا⁩ He's not here. She ⁧لَيْسَتْ⁩ laysat . ⁧لَيْسَتْ طَبِيبَةً⁩ He's not a doctor. us ⁧لَسْنَا⁩ lasnā . ⁧لَسْنَا مُهَنْدِسِينَ⁩ We're not engineers. you (m.) ⁧لَسْتُمْ⁩ lastum . ⁧لَسْتُمْ طُلَّابًا⁩ You're not students. vol (f.) ⁧لَسْتُنَّ⁩ lastunna  They (m.) ⁧لَيْسُوا⁩ laysū . ⁧لَيْسُوا مِصْرِيِّينَ⁩ They're not Egyptians. They (f.) ⁧لَسْنَ⁩ lasna  You two. ⁧لَسْتُمَا⁩ lastumā  the two of them (m.) ⁧لَيْسَا⁩ laysā  The two of them (f.) ⁧لَيْسَتَا⁩ laysatā The most frequent are ⁧لَسْتُ⁩ , ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ , ⁧لَيْسَتْ⁩ , ⁧لَسْنَا⁩ , ⁧لَيْسُوا⁩ : learn them first. Note the accusative of plural predicate: ⁧مُهَنْدِسِينَ⁩ ( -īna), ⁧طُلَّابًا⁩ , and for the female plural -ātin: . ⁧لَسْنَ مُهَنْدِسَاتٍ⁩ Before the Article ⁧لَيْسَتْ⁩ Takes one of the support: ⁧لَيْسَتِ الشَّقَّةُ كَبِيرَةً⁩ laysati š-šaqqatu kabīra . 4. ⁧لَا⁩ or ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ ? What you deny Particle Example a verb to the imperfect ⁧لَا⁩ . ⁧لَا أَسْكُنُ هُنَا⁩ I don't live here. a nominal sentence (without verb) ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ . ⁧لَسْتُ مِنْ هُنَا⁩ I'm not from here. Always ask yourself: is there a verb? If so, ⁧لَا⁩ ; if not, ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ . title: Days, hours, routine
text: Lesson overview Monday at 3.30 p.m., tomorrow morning morning, Tuesday morning: in this unit you learn the days of the week, months, ordinals and the way of saying the hour, which in Arabic uses the ordinal numbers to the female ( ⁧السَّاعَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ⁩ • the three sections, letter The third hour is the third hour. title: The perfect one; the denial withمَا‎
text: Lesson overview ⁧دَرَسْتُ⁩ I have studied it. ⁧ذَهَبَ⁩ It's gone. ⁧قَالَ الوَزِيرُ⁩ The Minister said: "" With the perfect ( ⁧المَاضِي⁩ al-māḍī ) short stories concluded actions: what you did yesterday, the weekend, last year. It is also the time of the news: almost every news begins with a verb to the perfect. In this unity learn conjugation, negation with ⁧مَا⁩ and the vocabulary to tell. Two weeks. Item Details Code A1-18 Level A1 · Module A1.4 Daily life Prerequisites A1-17 exceeded Estimated time 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 41–42 of the calendar) Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-18), voice synthesis script, tutor session in the second week Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. to combine the perfect with the singular and the persons (s) and (s) of their own; 2. recognize all other people of the perfect; 3. use the most frequent irregular perfects ( ⁧قَالَ⁩ , ⁧زَارَ⁩ , ⁧نَامَ⁩ , ⁧رَأَى⁩ ...) at least the third person and the first person; 4. deny the past with ⁧مَا⁩ and recognize denial with ⁧لَمْ⁩ ; 5. tell your day yesterday and your weekend in 70 words; 6. To understand a slow story to the past and a short story. Two-week plan. All forms with -you are -Io- ( ⁧ذَهَبْتُ⁩ , ⁧رَجَعْتُ⁩ , ⁧دَرَسْتُ⁩ ); con -ta sono ⁧فَعَلْتَ⁩ , ⁧فَهِمْتَ⁩ ); with -nā "Noi" ( ⁧أَكَلْنَا⁩ ). ⁧مَا خَرَجْتُ⁩ I have not gone out of the past: denial of the past. ⁧الدَّارِجَة⁩ is the name of Arabic spoken in Morocco: the film is in dialect, and that's why Luca asks the question. 2. The perfect: singular shapes The perfect form with suffixes added to a base (daras-, kataba-): no prefixes. It's the family of verbs "concavi": you will study it thoroughly in A2. ⁧كَانَ⁩ It was, it was. Enough for now in phrases like ⁧كَانَ الدَّرْسُ صَعْبًا⁩ The lesson was difficult and ⁧كُنْتُ فِي رُومَا⁩ I was in Rome. How ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ , puts the predicate to the accusative (A1-19). 6. The denial of the past: ⁧مَا⁩ Affirmative Negative Translation . ⁧ذَهَبْتُ⁩ . ⁧مَا ذَهَبْتُ⁩ I didn't go. . ⁧فَهِمَ الدَّرْسَ⁩ . ⁧مَا فَهِمَ الدَّرْسَ⁩ He didn't understand the lesson. . ⁧أَكَلْنَا⁩ . ⁧مَا أَكَلْنَا⁩ We didn't eat. ⁧مَا⁩ in front of the perfect is a correct denial of the standard Arabic, frequent in the educated speech and in many texts. To be recognized: . ⁧لَمْ⁩ In the prose journalistic and administrative past is more often denied with ⁧لَمْ⁩ + imperfect apocopate (without the final -u): ⁧لَمْ أَذْهَبْ⁩ I didn't go, ⁧لَمْ يَقُلْ⁩ • did not say: • The meaning is the same; form you will study it in A2. When you read ⁧لَمْ⁩ , think of the negative past. Do not confuse ⁧مَا⁩ denial (before a verb to the perfect) with ⁧مَا⁩ What? (in front of a name, A1-05): ⁧مَا فَهِمْتُ⁩ I don't understand. ⁧مَا هٰذَا؟⁩ What is it? 7. Telling: expressions of time ⁧أَمْسِ⁩ Yesterday. ⁧البَارِحَةَ⁩ Last night, yesterday. ⁧الأُسْبُوعَ المَاضِيَ⁩ Last week, it's gonna be okay. ⁧السَّنَةَ المَاضِيَةَ⁩ Last year. ⁧قَبْلَ أُسْبُوعٍ⁩ 1 week ago ⁧قَبْلَ سَنَتَيْنِ⁩ 2 years ago. ⁧مُنْذُ⁩ ( ⁧مُنْذُ سَنَةٍ⁩ (One year) · ⁧أَوَّلًا⁩ … ⁧ثُمَّ⁩ … ⁧بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ⁩ … ⁧فِي النِّهَايَةِ⁩ First... Then... After... at the end of the day. ⁧قَبْلَ⁩ and ⁧مُنْذُ⁩ . ⁧قَبْلَ⁩ + time = ⁧زُرْتُ القَاهِرَةَ قَبْلَ سَنَتَيْنِ⁩ I visited Cairo two years ago. ⁧مُنْذُ⁩ + time with imperfection = ⁧أَسْكُنُ فِي مِيلَانُو مُنْذُ سَنَةٍ⁩ I have lived in Milan for one year. 8. Dialogue 2 · The weekend Monday night, at the class. Arabic Transliteration Translation ⁧مَاذَا فَعَلْتُمْ فِي نِهَايَةِ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ ⁧الأُسْبُوعِ؟⁩ Salmā: māḏā faʿaltum fī nihāyati l- usbūʿ? Salmā: What did you do on the weekend? ⁧سَافَرْتُ إِلَى رُومَا مَعَ⁩ : ⁧يُوسُف⁩ ⁧زُرْنَا المَتَاحِفَ وَأَكَلْنَا فِي⁩ . ⁧سَمِير⁩ . ⁧مَطْعَمٍ تُونِسِيٍّ⁩ Yūsuf: sāfartu ilā Rūmā maʿa Samīr. zurnā l-matāḥifa wa-akalnā fī maṭʿamin tūnisī. Yūsuf: I went to Rome with Samīr. We visited the museums and ate in a Tunisian restaurant. ⁧وَهَلْ دَرَسْتُمَا؟⁩ ! ⁧جَمِيلٌ⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: ǧamīl! wa-hal darastumā? Salmā: Nice! And did you study (you two)? . ⁧مَا دَرَسْنَا كَثِيرًا⁩ … ⁧لَا⁩ : ⁧يُوسُف⁩ Yūsuf: lā… mā darasnā kaṯīran. Yūsuf: No... we didn't study much. ⁧وَأَنْتِ يَا مَارْيَا؟⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: wa-anti yā Māryā? Salmā: What about you, Maria? ⁧بَقِيتُ فِي⁩ . ⁧أَنَا مَا سَافَرْتُ⁩ : ⁧مَارْيَا⁩ . ⁧البَيْتِ وَكَتَبْتُ تَقْرِيرًا لِلشَّرِكَةِ⁩ Māryā: anā mā sāfartu. baqītu fī l- bayti wa-katabtu taqrīran li-š-šarika. I didn't leave. I stayed home and wrote a report for the company. ⁧وَهُدَى؟⁩ : ⁧سَلْمَى⁩ Salmā: wa-Hudā? Salmā: E Hudā? ⁧هِيَ عَمِلَتْ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ،⁩ : ⁧مَارْيَا⁩ ! ⁧وَيَوْمَ الأَحَدِ نَامَتْ حَتَّى الظُّهْرِ⁩ Māryā: hiya ʿamilat yawma s-sabt, wa-yawma l-aḥadi nāmat ḥattā ẓ- ẓuhr! She worked Saturday, and she slept until noon on Sunday! What to notice. ⁧فَعَلْتُمْ⁩ You have done this (you), ⁧دَرَسْتُمَا⁩ You have studied (you two), ⁧زُرْنَا⁩ We have visited the site (perfect irregular of ⁧زَارَ⁩ ). ⁧بَقِيتُ⁩ I have remained is another irregular verb (roots ⁧ب ق ي⁩ ): Learn it as a block. ⁧حَتَّى⁩ • up to and including. 9. The Perfect in the News News Translation . ⁧وَصَلَ وَزِيرُ الخَارِجِيَّةِ إِلَى القَاهِرَةِ أَمْسِ⁩ The Foreign Minister arrived yesterday in Cairo. … ⁧قَالَ المُتَحَدِّثُ بِاسْمِ الحُكُومَةِ إِنَّ⁩ The government spokesman said that... . ⁧اِجْتَمَعَ رَئِيسُ الوُزَرَاءِ مَعَ السَّفِيرِ الإِيطَالِيِّ⁩ The Prime Minister met with the Italian Ambassador. . ⁧زَارَ الرَّئِيسُ مَدِينَةَ البَصْرَةِ⁩ The president visited the city of Basra. The typical scheme: verb to perfect (3a singular person) + subject + complements + time. The first verb tells you what happened; the subject immediately after, who did. In B1 Read authentic news with this structure. ⁧قَالَ⁩ … ⁧إِنَّ⁩ • said that: the complete construction is in A2. 10. Pronunciation - You, -ta, -ti. Three different suffixes only in vowel: darastu, darast, darasti. Exercise with the B script until you distinguish them at first listening. The sukūn before the suffix. : ⁧دَرَسْتُ⁩ The s has no voice, daras-tu. Don't say darasatu. -ū and -ā Finals. darasū (they) darasā (they two): ū and ā long; the after-life wāw You don't read. ⁧قُلْتُ⁩ , ⁧زُرْتُ⁩ , ⁧نِمْتُ⁩ . Short voice: qultu , zurtu , nimtu . All 3long person: qāla , zāra , nāma . 11. For the taxi is also said. ⁧تَاكْسِي الدَّارِجَة⁩ ( o ⁧الدَّارِجَة المَغْرِبِيَّة⁩ ) is the Moroccan dialect; Similar terms are used in Algeria and Tunisia. 12. Yesterday.  . ⁧مَا فَهِمْتُ السُّؤَالَ، آسِف⁩ mā fahimtu s-suʾāl, āsif. I didn't understand the question, sorry.  ⁧كُنْتُ فِي القَاهِرَةِ قَبْلَ⁩ . ⁧سَنَتَيْنِ⁩ kuntu fī l-Qāhirati qabla sanatayn. I was in Cairo two years ago.  ⁧أَسْكُنُ هُنَا مُنْذُ ثَلَاثِ⁩ . ⁧سَنَوَاتٍ⁩ askunu hunā munḏu ṯalāṯi sanawāt. I've lived here for three years. I don't know, I didn't see anything.  ⁧حَضَرَ الطُّلَّابُ الدَّرْسَ،⁩ . ⁧لٰكِنِ الأُسْتَاذُ مَا جَاءَ⁩ ḥaḍara ṭ-ṭullābu d-dars, lākini l- ustāḏu mā ǧāʾa. I forgot my password.  . ⁧شَاهَدْنَا الأَخْبَارَ مَسَاءً⁩ šāhadnā l-aḫbāra masāʾan. The night we watched the news.  14. Reading Reading 1 · The journey of Laylā . ⁧ذَهَبَتْ مِنَ المَطَارِ إِلَى الفُنْدُقِ بِسَيَّارَةِ أُجْرَةٍ⁩ . ⁧وَصَلَتْ لَيْلَى إِلَى مِيلَانُو يَوْمَ الاِثْنَيْنِ صَبَاحًا⁩ ⁧بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ حَضَرَتِ المُؤْتَمَرَ فِي الجَامِعَةِ، وَسَمِعَتْ⁩ . ⁧فِي الفُنْدُقِ شَرِبَتْ قَهْوَةً وَقَرَأَتِ الأَخْبَارَ⁩ ⁧رَجَعَتْ إِلَى الفُنْدُقِ⁩ . ⁧مَسَاءً أَكَلَتْ فِي مَطْعَمٍ لُبْنَانِيٍّ مَعَ لُوكَا وَسَلْمَى⁩ . ⁧كَلِمَةَ وَزِيرِ الدَّاخِلِيَّةِ⁩ . ⁧مُتَأَخِّرَةً، وَكَتَبَتْ مَقَالَتَهَا لِلْجَرِيدَةِ قَبْلَ النَّوْمِ⁩ Reading 2 · A wrong day ⁧فِي⁩ . ⁧مَا شَرِبْتُ القَهْوَةَ، وَمَا أَكَلْتُ شَيْئًا⁩ . ⁧أَمْسِ مَا سَمِعْتُ المُنَبِّهَ، وَخَرَجْتُ مِنَ البَيْتِ مُتَأَخِّرًا⁩ . ⁧ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى العَمَلِ بِالمِتْرُو⁩ ! ⁧هِيَ أَمَامَ بَيْتِ أُخْتِي⁩ : ⁧الشَّارِعِ مَا وَجَدْتُ سَيَّارَتِي، ثُمَّ تَذَكَّرْتُ⁩ ⁧مَسَاءً كُنْتُ مُتْعَبًا جِدًّا، وَمَا⁩ . ⁧فِي المَكْتَبِ نَسِيتُ كَلِمَةَ السِّرِّ لِلْحَاسُوبِ، وَمَا كَتَبْتُ التَّقْرِيرَ⁩ ! ⁧الحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ، اليَوْمَ يَوْمٌ جَدِيدٌ⁩ . ⁧فَهِمْتُ الدَّرْسَ الجَدِيدَ⁩ Glossary: ⁧المُنَبِّه⁩ al-munabbih 16. Listening Script A · Dialog 2 ⁧زُرْنَا المَتَاحِفَ وَأَكَلْنَا فِي مَطْعَمٍ⁩ . ⁧مَاذَا فَعَلْتُمْ فِي نِهَايَةِ الأُسْبُوعِ؟ سَافَرْتُ إِلَى رُومَا مَعَ سَمِير⁩ ⁧بَقِيتُ فِي⁩ . ⁧وَأَنْتِ يَا مَارْيَا؟ أَنَا مَا سَافَرْتُ⁩ . ⁧مَا دَرَسْنَا كَثِيرًا⁩ … ⁧وَهَلْ دَرَسْتُمَا؟ لَا⁩ ! ⁧جَمِيلٌ⁩ . ⁧تُونِسِيٍّ⁩ . ⁧البَيْتِ وَكَتَبْتُ تَقْرِيرًا لِلشَّرِكَةِ⁩ Script B · Me, you or you? . ⁧دَرَسْتُ كَثِيرًا⁩ . ⁧١⁩ ⁧هَلْ فَهِمْتَ؟⁩ . ⁧٢⁩ ⁧أَيْنَ كُنْتِ أَمْسِ؟⁩ . ⁧٣⁩ . ⁧كَتَبَتِ الرِّسَالَةَ⁩ . ⁧٤⁩ . ⁧مَا رَأَيْتُ شَيْئًا⁩ . ⁧٥⁩ . ⁧ذَهَبُوا إِلَى المَطَارِ⁩ . ⁧٦⁩ . ⁧وَصَلْنَا مُتَأَخِّرِينَ⁩ . ⁧٧⁩ ⁧مَتَى رَجَعْتَ؟⁩ . ⁧٨⁩ Script C · News ⁧زَارَ الوَفْدُ المِصْرِيُّ⁩ . ⁧وَصَلَ وَزِيرُ الخَارِجِيَّةِ الإِيطَالِيُّ إِلَى تُونِسَ أَمْسِ، وَاجْتَمَعَ مَعَ رَئِيسِ الحُكُومَةِ⁩ . ⁧مَا حَضَرَ الوَزِيرُ المُؤْتَمَرَ، وَقَالَ المُتَحَدِّثُ بِاسْمِ الوِزَارَةِ إِنَّهُ مَشْغُولٌ⁩ . ⁧مِيلَانُو الأُسْبُوعَ المَاضِيَ⁩ 17. Oral production 1. Yesterday. Tell the tutor your day yesterday in a minute; the tutor interrupts you with questions ( ⁧مَتَى؟ مَعَ مَنْ؟⁩ ⁧لِمَاذَا؟⁩ ). 2. The weekend (second week): interview the tutor on his weekend using forms in -ta / -ti; then sum up what you did to the 3per person. 3. News report. Read the C script as a speaker, then rephrase every news with your own words. 18. Typical errors Error Correction ⁧أَمْسِ أَذْهَبُ⁩ : ⁧أَمْسِ ذَهَبْتُ⁩ finished action → perfect  ⁧هِيَ ذَهَبَتْهِيَ ذَهَبَ⁩ ⁧دَرَسُو⁩ without alif : ⁧دَرَسُوا⁩ the alif is written but you can't read ⁧قَالْتُ⁩ : ⁧قُلْتُ⁩ concave shortens the base  ⁧مَا ذَهَبْتُلَا ذَهَبْتُ⁩ ( o ⁧لَمْ أَذْهَبْ⁩ ): ⁧لَا⁩ denies the imperfect  ⁧ذَهَبَ الطُّلَّابُذَهَبُوا الطُّلَّابُ⁩ darasatu for I have studied darastu: the s has no vowel Confound ⁧مَا⁩ Not further worked than hot-rolled, hot-drawn or cold-rolled (cold-reduced) ⁧مَا⁩ What's going on? ⁧مَا⁩ + perfect = negation; ⁧مَا⁩ + name = question 19. title: Cases (iʿrāb): nominative, accusative, genitive
text: Lesson overview From A1-01 read the final vowels of the words: -u in ⁧البَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ⁩ , -i ⁧فِي البَيْتِ⁩ -a in ⁧أَقْرَأُ الجَرِيدَةَ⁩ . It's the case endings, and the system that rules is called iʿrāb ( ⁧إِعْرَاب⁩ ). In this unit, you collect what you have seen in a single picture, unity by unity: three cases, their functions, the forms in the different types of names, and two new words that govern them, ⁧كَانَ⁩ and ⁧إِنَّ⁩ . You'll also learn to read a text with all sorts of endings, like a radio journalist, and to recognize cases in unvocal texts. Two weeks; close the form A1.4. What are the cases An Arabic name changes the final vowel according to its function in the sentence. There are three cases: Case Arabic name Desinence (determined - indefinite) Sign Name ⁧مَرْفُوع⁩ marfūʿ -u · -un ⁧ٌـ⁩ · ⁧ُـ⁩ Accused ⁧مَنْصُوب⁩ manṣūb -a · -an ⁧ًـ⁩ · ⁧َـ⁩ Genitive ⁧مَجْرُور⁩ maǧrūr -i · -in ⁧ٍـ⁩ · ⁧ِـ⁩ Because they exist. In Latin and German the cases allow you to move words without losing sense; in Arabic is the same. In the modern spoken language, desinences have almost disappeared and the order of words has become more fixed; Standard Arabic keeps them in vocalized spelling and formal reading. Three reading levels. 1) Pause: no endings at the end of the sentence, which is how you have read the transliteration so far. 2) Complete: all endings except the last before the break (notes, official speeches, Koran). 3) Mixed: the most widespread in the educated speech, with desinences at the points where they serve to ligament or sense. In A1 we ask you to understand the full reading and at least produce the mixed one. 2. Reading · A Letter From Salmā to his mother ⁧كَانَ الأُسْبُوعُ⁩ . ⁧كَيْفَ حَالُكِ وَحَالُ أَبِي؟ نَحْنُ بِخَيْرٍ، وَالحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ⁩ . ⁧السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ يَا أُمِّي⁩ : ⁧فِي صَفِّي طُلَّابٌ مِنْ بِلَادٍ مُخْتَلِفَةٍ⁩ . ⁧المَاضِي طَوِيلًا وَصَعْبًا، لِأَنَّ الطُّلَّابَ كَثِيرُونَ هٰذِهِ السَّنَةَ⁩ ⁧إِنَّ هٰذَا الصَّفَّ مُمْتَازٌ،⁩ . ⁧شُرْطِيٌّ إِيطَالِيٌّ، وَمُتَرْجِمٌ مَغْرِبِيٌّ، وَطَالِبَانِ مِنْ تُونِسَ وَالمَغْرِبِ⁩ ⁧يَوْمَ الجُمُعَةِ زُرْنَا صَدِيقَةَ عَادِل المِصْرِيَّةَ فِي بَيْتِهَا الجَدِيدِ، وَأَكَلْنَا⁩ . ⁧وَالطُّلَّابُ يَدْرُسُونَ كَثِيرًا⁩ ⁧نَحْنُ نَزُورُكُمْ فِي القَاهِرَةِ⁩ . ⁧نُور تَتَكَلَّمُ العَرَبِيَّةَ جَيِّدًا الآنَ، وَتَسْأَلُ عَنْكِ دَائِمًا⁩ . ⁧طَعَامًا مِصْرِيًّا⁩ ⁧سَلَامِي⁩ . ⁧لَيْسَتِ الرِّحْلَةُ رَخِيصَةً، لٰكِنَّ العَائِلَةَ أَهَمُّ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ⁩ . ⁧فِي الصَّيْفِ، إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ⁩ . ⁧بِنْتُكِ سَلْمَى⁩ . ⁧إِلَى أَبِي وَطَارِق⁩ 14. Listening Script A · Two readings Reading 1 (complete), read 2 (Pause). Same text. ⁧قَرَأُوا نُصُوصًا قَصِيرَةً، وَكَتَبُوا⁩ . ⁧كَانَ الجَوُّ بَارِدًا أَمْسِ، لٰكِنَّ الطُّلَّابَ ذَهَبُوا إِلَى الجَامِعَةِ صَبَاحًا⁩ . ⁧رَسَائِلَ إِلَى أَصْدِقَائِهِمْ⁩ Who reads: the first time he pronounces all the terminations ( kāna l-ǧawwu bāridan amsi, lākinna ṭ-ṭullāba ḏahabū… ); the second omits them at the end of the group ( kāna l-ǧaww bārid ams, lākinna ṭ-ṭullāb ḏahabū ila l-ǧāmiʿa ṣabāḥan… ). In the vocal synthesis app you will usually listen to a mixed reading. Script B · Dictation with case endings . ⁧البَيْتُ الكَبِيرُ جَمِيلٌ⁩ . ⁧١⁩ . ⁧ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى المَكْتَبِ صَبَاحًا⁩ . ⁧٢⁩ . ⁧قَرَأَ المُدِيرُ التَّقْرِيرَ⁩ . ⁧٣⁩ . ⁧كَانَ الدَّرْسُ صَعْبًا⁩ . ⁧٤⁩ . ⁧إِنَّ الطَّالِبَةَ مُجْتَهِدَةٌ⁩ . ⁧٥⁩ . ⁧تَكَلَّمْتُ مَعَ المُهَنْدِسِينَ⁩ . ⁧٦⁩ 15. Oral production 1. Speaker reading. Read with complete desinences the news of A1-10 (section 13) and the C script of A1-18. Record and compare with vocal synthesis. 2. Explain to tutor (second week): choose three sentences from the letter of Salmā and explains it by voice, in English or in simple Arabic, because every word has its desinence. The tutor then asks you two questions: "trabocchetto" of the type of exercise 6. 3. Mixed reading. Read a text from A1-13 in the way you would speak to an Arabic colleague: desinences where serve, pause at the end of groups. 16. Typical errors Error Correction ⁧كَانَ الجَوُّ بَارِدٌ⁩ : ⁧كَانَ الجَوُّ بَارِدًا⁩ predicate of ⁧كَانَ⁩ to the defendant ⁧إِنَّ الجَوُّ بَارِدٌ⁩ : ⁧إِنَّ الجَوَّ بَارِدٌ⁩ subject of ⁧إِنَّ⁩ to the defendant  ⁧رَأَيْتُ المُدَرِّسِينَرَأَيْتُ المُدَرِّسُونَ⁩  ⁧رَأَيْتُ المُدَرِّسَاتِرَأَيْتُ المُدَرِّسَاتَ⁩ ⁧فِي مَدَارِسٍ⁩ : ⁧فِي مَدَارِسَ⁩ diptototo without tanwīn, genitive in -a Deduce the subject only from the position in a vocalized text Look at the desinence: -u = subject Pronouncing desinence even before break Break falls 17. Flashcard Deck A1, tag A1-19: 23 rumors. Add a card with the function frame (section 2) and one with the name type table (section 5): recite them as tables. 18. Unit verification Twenty points; Exceeding at least 16. A · Functions (6 (paragraphs) (i) Case and function of the bold word: 1. ⁧قَرَأْتُ⁩ ⁧الجَرِيدَةَ⁩ · 2. ⁧فِي⁩ ⁧الشَّارِعِ⁩ · 3. ⁧المُدِيرُ⁩ ⁧مَشْغُولٌ⁩ · 4. ⁧كَانَ الطَّقْسُ⁩ ⁧جَمِيلًا⁩ · 5. ⁧إِنَّ⁩ ⁧المُشْكِلَةَ⁩ ⁧كَبِيرَةٌ⁩ · 6. ⁧رَجَعْتُ⁩ ⁧لَيْلًا⁩ B · Desinences (6 (paragraphs) (i) Vocalize: 7. ⁧ذهب الموظف إلى البنك⁩ · 8. ⁧كتبت رسالة طويلة⁩ · 9. ⁧كان البيت⁩ ⁧قديما⁩ · 10. ⁧إن الشرطة في المطار⁩ · 11. ⁧سيارة المدير الجديدة⁩ · 12. ⁧تكلمنا مع المترجمين⁩ C · Forms (4 (paragraphs) 13. "Two interpreters" to the genitive · 14. The students are charged with the prosecution. 15. Your father's at the charge. 16. In schools ( ⁧مَدَارِس⁩ D · Understanding (4 (paragraphs) 17. . ⁧سَاعَدَ الطَّبِيبَ المُمَرِّضُ⁩ · 18. . ⁧أَعْرِفُ أَنَّ الاِجْتِمَاعَ غَدًا⁩ · 19. ⁧لَيْسَتِ⁩ . ⁧المَحَطَّةُ بَعِيدَةً⁩ · 20. . ⁧كَانَ الطُّلَّابُ غَائِبِينَ⁩ 19. To switch to the module test A1.4 • ☐ Verification ≥ 16/20. • ☐ You can explain the desinence of each word in a well-known sentence. • ☐ You have read the letter of Salmā with complete terminations to 40 words per minute. • ☐ Verifications A1-16 → A1-18 They're out of date. • ☐ Check with filtered deck A1-16 → A1-19 That's it.

title: Review and examination A1
text: Lesson overview The last three weeks of the level serve to consolidate, measure and close gaps. There is no new grammar: review the vocabulary for areas, review the grammatical framework, read three long texts, listen to two cumulative dialogues, do an exam simulation and, in the week 48, support the exam A1 (Part III). Item Details Code A1-20 Level A1 · Review Prerequisites Module testing A1.1 → A1.4 Exceeded Estimated time 18–20 hours · three weeks (weeks 46–48 of the calendar) Materials All volume, Anki deck A1 complete, Reference Grammar (Part V), progress log, oral simulation tutor Targets. At the end of the three weeks: 1. recognize and use vocabulary A1 of all areas; 2. apply without hesitation the grammatical framework structures of the section 3; 3. read teaching texts vocabulary 120–150 words at least 40 words per minute and answer questions details; 4. understand slow didactic dialogues on daily life, work, family and city; 5. write 80 understandable words on a well-known theme; 6. support a prepared conversation of 10 minutes; 7. pass the exam A1 (≥ 70%, every skill ≥ 60%). Three-week plan. Week Day Activity 46 1 Vocabulary 1–4 (section 2) · Full Anki 46 2 Vocabulary 5–11 · grammatical framework (section 3), part 1 46 3 Grammatical framework, part 2 · text 1 46 4 Text 2 · dialogue A 46 5 Text 3 • Dialogue B • Production 1 (section 7) 46 6 Examination simulation (section) 8), under real conditions 46 7 Simulation correction · list of gaps in the register 47 1–2 Grammar gaps: return to the units indicated by the correction 47 3 Timed reading of the three texts (section 6) 47 4 Production 2 · Guided rewriting of production 1 47 5 Targeted Listening: scripts of units corresponding to gaps 47 6 Interview prepared with the tutor (exercise 9) 47 7 Active rest: only Anki (error cards) 48 — Examination A1 (Part III) in two half days 1. How to Review Anki. Deck A1 complete, every day, with a deck filtered on the wrong cards in the last 30 days. Create a card for each recurring error of the simulation. • Aloud. Each review text is read twice: in pause and with the endings. • Register. Write down in the Excel file the simulation scores for skill: they are the basis of the plan of week 47. • Tutor. Oral simulation should be done with a native speaker: pronunciation does not evaluate itself. 2. The vocabulary A1 by areas The keywords of each area, with the unity where you studied them. Some words come from the Level 0. The complete list of the vocabulary A1 is in Appendix B. Scope Keywords Unit 1. Greetings and courtesy ⁧السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ، صَبَاحُ الخَيْرِ، كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟، شُكْرًا، عَفْوًا، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، آسِف،⁩ ⁧لَا بَأْسَ، تَفَضَّلْ، إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ⁩ A1-01, A1-05 2. Persons and professions ⁧طَالِب، مُدَرِّس، شُرْطِيّ، ضَابِط، مُتَرْجِم، صَحَفِيّ، طَبِيب، مُهَنْدِس، مُحَامٍ،⁩ ⁧مُحَلِّل، مُوَظَّف، مُدِير⁩ A1-02, A1-15 3. Family ⁧أَب، أُمّ، أَخ، أُخْت، زَوْج، زَوْجَة، اِبْن، بِنْت، عَمّ، خَال، جَدّ، أُسْرَة⁩ A1-09 4. Nationality and languages ⁧عَرَبِيّ، إِيطَالِيّ، مِصْرِيّ، مَغْرِبِيّ، سُورِيّ، عِرَاقِيّ، لُبْنَانِيّ، أَجْنَبِيّ، جِنْسِيَّة،⁩ ⁧لُغَة، مُقِيم⁩ A1-07 5. Home and City ⁧بَيْت، شَقَّة، غُرْفَة، مَطْبَخ، شَارِع، حَيّ، مَيْدَان، مَحَطَّة، سُوق، مَطْعَم، فُنْدُق،⁩ ⁧حَافِلَة⁩ A1-04, A1-08, A1-16 6. Institutions ⁧وِزَارَة، وَزِير، رَئِيس، حُكُومَة، سَفَارَة، سَفِير، مَجْلِس، بَلَدِيَّة، مَرْكَزُ الشُّرْطَةِ،⁩ ⁧عَاصِمَة⁩ A1-10 7. Articles and documents ⁧كِتَاب، قَلَم، هَاتِف، حَاسُوب، مِفْتَاح، حَقِيبَة، جَوَازُ سَفَرٍ، بِطَاقَة، رِسَالَة،⁩ ⁧تَقْرِير⁩ A1-05, A1-13 8. Time ⁧يَوْم، أُسْبُوع، شَهْر، سَنَة، سَاعَة، دَقِيقَة، اليَوْمَ، أَمْسِ، غَدًا، صَبَاحًا، مَسَاءً،⁩ ⁧السَّبْت⁩ … ⁧الأَحَد⁩ A1-06, A1-11, A1-17 9. Frequent verbs ⁧يَدْرُسُ، يَعْمَلُ، يَسْكُنُ، يَذْهَبُ، يَرْجِعُ، يَكْتُبُ، يَقْرَأُ، يَعْرِفُ، يَفْهَمُ، يَتَكَلَّمُ،⁩ ⁧يُرِيدُ، يَقُولُ، يَزُورُ، يَصِلُ⁩ A1-13, A1-14, A1-18 10. Adjective ⁧كَبِير، صَغِير، جَدِيد، قَدِيم، جَمِيل، طَوِيل، قَرِيب، بَعِيد، سَهْل، صَعْب، مُهِمّ،⁩ ⁧مَشْغُول⁩ A1-03 11. Functional words ⁧فِي، عَلَى، مِنْ، إِلَى، مَعَ، عِنْدَ، بَيْنَ، هَلْ، مَا، مَنْ، أَيْنَ، مَتَى، كَمْ، لِمَاذَا، لَا،⁩ A1-06, A1-08, ⁧لَيْسَ، لٰكِنْ، لِأَنَّ⁩ A1-14 Exercise 1. For each area write in a minute, without looking, all the words you remember; then check and add in Anki a tag "Return" to forgotten words. 3. Text 2 · A news (past) ⁧وَصَلَ وَزِيرُ الدَّاخِلِيَّةِ الإِيطَالِيُّ إِلَى تُونِسَ صَبَاحَ أَمْسِ فِي زِيَارَةٍ رَسْمِيَّةٍ قَصِيرَةٍ،⁩ — ⁧تُونِسُ⁩ ⁧كَانَ وَزِيرُ الدَّاخِلِيَّةِ التُّونِسِيُّ فِي المَطَارِ،⁩ . ⁧وَهِيَ الزِّيَارَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ لِلْوَزِيرِ إِلَى تُونِسَ هٰذِهِ السَّنَةَ⁩ ⁧وَذَهَبَ الوَزِيرَانِ مِنَ المَطَارِ إِلَى مَقَرِّ الوِزَارَةِ، وَاجْتَمَعَا هُنَاكَ سَاعَتَيْنِ، وَتَكَلَّمَا عَنْ أَمْنِ⁩ ⁧بَعْدَ الاِجْتِمَاعِ قَالَ الوَزِيرُ الإِيطَالِيُّ⁩ . ⁧الحُدُودِ وَالهِجْرَةِ غَيْرِ القَانُونِيَّةِ وَالتَّعَاوُنِ بَيْنَ البَلَدَيْنِ⁩ ⁧وَقَالَ⁩ . ⁧لِلصَّحَفِيِّينَ إِنَّ العَلَاقَاتِ بَيْنَ إِيطَالِيَا وَتُونِسَ مُمْتَازَةٌ، وَإِنَّ التَّعَاوُنَ بَيْنَهُمَا مُهِمٌّ جِدًّا⁩ ⁧مَا⁩ . ⁧الوَزِيرُ التُّونِسِيُّ إِنَّ الشُّرْطَةَ التُّونِسِيَّةَ تَعْمَلُ كَثِيرًا عَلَى الحُدُودِ، لٰكِنَّ المُشْكِلَةَ كَبِيرَةٌ⁩ ⁧تَكَلَّمَ الوَزِيرُ الإِيطَالِيُّ عَنْ أَرْقَامِ المُهَاجِرِينَ، وَقَالَ إِنَّ هُنَاكَ اجْتِمَاعًا آخَرَ فِي رُومَا الشَّهْرَ⁩ ⁧بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ زَارَ الوَفْدُ الإِيطَالِيُّ مِينَاءَ المَدِينَةِ، وَتَكَلَّمَ مَعَ ضُبَّاطِ الشُّرْطَةِ هُنَاكَ،⁩ . ⁧القَادِمَ⁩ ⁧وَفِي المَسَاءِ أَكَلَ الوَزِيرُ فِي السَّفَارَةِ الإِيطَالِيَّةِ مَعَ السَّفِيرِ،⁩ . ⁧وَسَأَلَهُمْ عَنْ مَشَاكِلِ عَمَلِهِمْ⁩ . ⁧وَرَجَعَ إِلَى رُومَا صَبَاحَ اليَوْمِ⁩ Glossary: ⁧صَبَاحَ أَمْسِ⁩ Yesterday morning ⁧زِيَارَة⁩ Visit ⁧الهِجْرَة غَيْر القَانُونِيَّة⁩ "Illegal immigration" · ⁧التَّعَاوُن⁩ • cooperation ⁧البَلَدَيْنِ⁩ The two countries (dual) ⁧العَلَاقَات⁩ The report shall be completed by: ⁧مِينَاء⁩ Port ⁧المُهَاجِرِينَ⁩ "Migrants" ⁧صَبَاحَ اليَوْمِ⁩ This morning.
